name: Silicon atom
role: Supplies the electronic states from which semiconductor behavior is engineered.
description: Silicon begins the atlas at the scale of matter. A neutral atom has fourteen electrons, with four in its outer occupied shell. That electron structure matters because neighboring silicon atoms can share electrons in bonds, creating a solid with electronic behavior unlike either an isolated atom or a metal. The atlas represents the nucleus and electron probability regions schematically; electrons do not orbit on neat planetary tracks. An atom is also not a digital bit. Computation appears only after enormous numbers of atoms are arranged into materials, devices, circuits, and controlled signals. Follow the lattice connection to see the first collective structure in that chain.

specs.label: Atomic number
specs.context: Number of protons; also electrons in a neutral atom.

specs.label: Outer-shell electrons
specs.context: The 3s²3p² ground-state configuration.

specs.label: Representation
specs.context: Displayed electron regions are explanatory, not trajectories.

interfaces.name: Neighboring atoms
interfaces.signal: Shared electronic states and chemical bonding

tradeoff: Atomic properties constrain material choice. Fabrication must control defects and interfaces as well as the element itself.
whyAI: An individual silicon atom performs no AI operation. Its collective electronic behavior makes controllable hardware possible.
scale: Subnanometer; atom drawing is conceptual
mechanism: Identify the nucleus and the fourteen-electron structure of a neutral silicon atom.
Focus on the four outer-shell electrons that participate in bonding with neighbors.
Join many atoms to obtain collective material behavior, then continue to devices and circuits.
misconception: A silicon atom is not a miniature digital processor; computation requires organized devices, circuitry, and controlled signals.

check.question: Where does a silicon atom become a digital bit?
options: An isolated atom always stores one bit
Only through an engineered physical encoding in a larger device or circuit
Each outer electron is a permanent binary register
check.explanation: Bits are information encodings. The atlas moves from atomic properties to a circuit that deliberately represents two states.

science.title: Charge bookkeeping
science.explanation: Z counts protons and Nₑ counts electrons. Neutral silicon has Z = Nₑ = 14; gaining or losing electrons changes charge without changing the element.
science.assumptions: Bookkeeping relation for an isolated atom or ion; it does not describe quantum orbital shapes.

name: Diamond-cubic silicon lattice
role: Organizes atoms into a repeatable semiconductor crystal.
description: In crystalline silicon, each atom bonds tetrahedrally to four nearest neighbors. Repeating this arrangement produces the diamond-cubic structure rather than a simple stack of square grids. The regular potential of this crystal gives electrons extended states, while defects and vibrations interrupt transport. The visible rods in the atlas stand for bonds, not literal mechanical struts, and the unit-cell outline is a coordinate aid. Crystal orientation influences how surfaces are exposed and how a device is fabricated. Zooming out from this ordered network leads to a wafer; zooming toward an interface reveals why atomic roughness becomes consequential when a transistor channel is only nanometers thick.

specs.label: Lattice constant
specs.context: Room-temperature conventional cubic cell edge, rounded.

specs.label: Nearest-neighbor distance
specs.context: Different from the lattice constant.

specs.label: Coordination
specs.context: Tetrahedral covalent bonding.

tradeoff: Order supports reproducible behavior. Strain, defects, and surface roughness alter the same electronic structure.
whyAI: Crystal quality helps devices switch predictably across a chip. Predictability is necessary for billions of coordinated logic operations.
scale: ≈0.2–0.5 nm atomic spacings; enlarged lattice fragment
mechanism: Place four nearest neighbors around a silicon atom in a tetrahedral arrangement.
Repeat the bonding pattern in three dimensions to form the diamond-cubic crystal.
Inspect a surface or interface, where the repeating pattern ends and device behavior becomes sensitive to atomic structure.
misconception: The ≈0.543 nm lattice constant is the conventional cell edge, not the distance between nearest neighboring atoms.

check.question: What does the silicon lattice constant measure?
options: The conventional cubic cell edge
The diameter of a finished transistor
The energy needed to free an electron
check.explanation: The nearest-neighbor separation is smaller, approximately 0.235 nm. The two numbers describe different geometry.

science.title: Diamond-cubic nearest neighbors
science.explanation: The nearest-neighbor distance follows from the diamond-cubic basis. With a ≈ 0.543 nm, dₙₙ ≈ 0.235 nm and the ideal atomic density is about 5 × 10²² cm⁻³.
science.assumptions: Ideal diamond-cubic silicon with eight effective atoms in the conventional cubic cell; temperature, strain, and defects change actual geometry.

name: Energy bands and carriers
role: Explains how a semiconductor can be electrically controlled.
description: A crystal offers ranges of allowed electron energies, called bands, separated by forbidden ranges. In silicon, the valence and conduction bands are separated by an energy gap. Supplying energy can create a mobile conduction electron and a corresponding hole in the valence band. The hole is a useful description of an absent electron in the many-electron solid, not a second kind of tiny positive atom. Band diagrams plot energy, sometimes against position; their vertical axis is not physical height. Gate fields and doping reshape the occupancy and alignment of these states. That connection lets materials physics become a voltage-controlled current in a transistor.

specs.label: Silicon band gap
specs.context: Near room temperature; varies with temperature.

specs.label: Carrier types
specs.context: Collective semiconductor transport description.

specs.label: Diagram axis
specs.context: Band separation is not a spatial distance.

tradeoff: A gap enables an off state. Thermal excitation and unwanted leakage prevent ideal isolation.
whyAI: AI hardware depends on distinct, reliable electrical states. Band engineering supports that distinction before any arithmetic exists.

sources.title: MIT 3.091 — Band Diagrams, Semiconductors, and Doping
MIT 3.23 — Semiconductor Statistics and Mass Action

scale: Energy-space schematic; eV rather than meters
mechanism: Locate the occupied valence states and available conduction states on an energy diagram.
Add enough energy to create a conduction electron and corresponding valence-band hole.
Change fields or doping to alter state occupancy and transport conditions inside a device.
misconception: The gap between bands is an energy interval, not an empty physical layer sandwiched inside silicon.

check.question: What is the vertical distance in an ordinary band diagram?
options: A physical insulating gap
An electron flight distance
An energy difference
check.explanation: Band diagrams organize allowed electronic energies. They do not depict bands as material shelves.

science.title: Thermal carrier generation
science.explanation: N_C and N_V describe the effective state densities near the conduction and valence edges. A larger gap suppresses the equilibrium intrinsic carrier population, while higher temperature generally increases it.
science.assumptions: Nondegenerate semiconductor in thermal equilibrium; material parameters and band gap can depend on temperature.

name: Donor and acceptor doping
role: Changes carrier populations by introducing selected impurity atoms.
description: Doping deliberately changes a semiconductor by incorporating a small population of other elements. In silicon, a donor such as phosphorus can supply an electron; an acceptor such as boron creates a hole in the carrier description. The crystal remains a material with extended electronic states, rather than isolated dopant atoms acting as individual switches. N-type and p-type describe the dominant mobile carrier, not a permanently charged bulk object. Spatially different doping regions help establish junctions and useful terminal behavior. Modern devices may combine heavily doped source/drain regions with lightly doped channels, so a single uniform sprinkling is only a teaching view, not a production doping map.

specs.label: Donor example
specs.context: Group-V atom in a silicon host.

specs.label: Acceptor example
specs.context: Group-III atom in a silicon host.

specs.label: Quantity to specify
specs.context: An actual device requires process-specific characterization.

tradeoff: More carriers can reduce resistance. Impurities and statistical variation can also degrade transport and uniformity.
whyAI: Doping helps make complementary switching networks possible. Those networks become memory, arithmetic, and control circuitry.
scale: Atomic substitutions within nanometer-to-micrometer device regions
mechanism: Replace selected silicon host atoms with donor or acceptor species.
Allow these species to change the available mobile electron or hole populations.
Arrange different regions spatially to obtain useful junctions and transistor terminal behavior.
misconception: N-type does not mean the bulk material carries an uncompensated permanent negative charge; it identifies the majority mobile carrier.

check.question: What distinguishes n-type silicon?
options: Its majority mobile carriers are electrons
Every atom is negatively charged
It contains no holes at any temperature
check.explanation: N-type refers to which mobile carriers dominate. Ionized dopants and the rest of the solid also participate in charge balance.

science.title: Mass action and donor control
science.equation: np = nᵢ²; n ≈ N_D; p ≈ nᵢ² / N_D
science.explanation: For donor-dominated silicon, the majority electron density follows the activated donors while the minority hole density decreases. This connects atomic substitution to measurable conductivity.
science.assumptions: Thermal equilibrium, full donor ionization, negligible compensation, N_D much larger than nᵢ, and nondegenerate statistics; heavily doped materials require a better model.

name: P–n junction and depletion region
role: Creates an internal electric field between differently doped regions.
description: When p-type and n-type regions meet, carrier concentration differences drive diffusion. Mobile charge redistributes near the interface, leaving a region whose fixed ionized dopants produce an electric field. At thermal equilibrium, drift and diffusion balance, so the internal field does not provide a perpetual power source. The depletion approximation models this region as mostly depleted of mobile carriers and makes its electrostatics easier to understand. Applied voltage changes the barrier and charge distribution. Junctions appear in transistor bodies and isolation structures as well as diodes. They help explain why a transistor is more than three metal terminals attached to an otherwise featureless silicon block.

specs.label: Equilibrium
specs.context: No net equilibrium current.

specs.label: Depletion region
specs.context: Also depends on doping and material properties.

specs.label: Built-in potential
specs.context: Not a free external voltage source.

tradeoff: Junctions provide useful isolation. Their capacitance and leakage add delay and power costs.
whyAI: Electrical isolation keeps nearby circuit functions independent. Its nonideal behavior contributes to chip power and timing limits.
scale: Device-scale junction; width is illustrative and bias-dependent
mechanism: Bring differently doped p-type and n-type regions into contact.
Let carriers redistribute until fixed dopant charge creates an opposing electric field.
At equilibrium, balance carrier diffusion with field-driven drift; applied bias shifts that balance.
misconception: The built-in junction field is not a battery that can supply unlimited power to an external circuit.

check.question: What happens to net current at thermal equilibrium?
options: It grows without external energy
Drift and diffusion contributions balance
The depletion region becomes a metallic short
check.explanation: Internal carrier motion and opposing contributions can exist while the equilibrium net current is zero.

science.title: Built-in junction potential
science.equation: V_bi = (k_B T / q) ln(N_A N_D / nᵢ²)
science.explanation: The internal potential follows from the different equilibrium carrier populations. N_A and N_D are acceptor and donor densities, while k_B T / q is the thermal voltage.
science.assumptions: Ideal equilibrium junction with nondegenerate regions and effective ionized doping densities; this is not an externally available battery voltage.

name: Wafer and fabrication hierarchy
role: Provides the shared substrate on which many integrated circuits are fabricated.
description: A wafer is a thin, polished slice of highly purified crystalline silicon. Many die patterns are processed across its surface together before testing and singulation separate usable chips. Device formation near the surface is commonly described as front end of line, or FEOL; local connections bridge devices to the back end of line, or BEOL, wiring stack. These labels describe manufacturing regions, not software front ends and back ends. Repeated patterning, deposition, removal, cleaning, and measurement build the structures layer by layer. The atlas compresses this long chain into a navigable cross section so viewers can connect a macroscopic wafer to the tiny electrical structures it carries.

specs.label: Example wafer diameter
specs.context: Widely used advanced-logic manufacturing format; not universal.

specs.label: Thickness
specs.context: General introductory wafer description, not a procurement specification.

specs.label: Hierarchy
specs.context: Test and assembly intervene between stages.

tradeoff: Larger useful die area can reduce unit cost. Defects, edge loss, and yield complicate that benefit.
whyAI: AI accelerators emerge from this manufacturing platform. Wafer yield and die size influence the cost of available compute.

sources.title: Intel — Semiconductors and Intel: An Introduction
Electronic Materials and Fabrication — Productivity and Process Yield

scale: 300 mm example wafer carrying microscopic structures
mechanism: Begin with a polished crystalline wafer that supports many die locations.
Build device regions and wiring through repeated patterning and material-processing stages.
Test the fabricated structures, separate die, and assemble usable die into packages.
misconception: A wafer, a die, and a package are different objects; one patterned wafer normally contains many die.

check.question: Which order follows physical integration?
options: Package → atom → wafer
Wafer → fabricated die → package
Metal gate → data center → dopant
check.explanation: Die are fabricated across a wafer and later separated for assembly. Testing and yield determine which proceed.

science.title: A first defect-yield model
science.explanation: If random fatal defects occur at density D₀ per unit area, larger die area increases the chance of encountering one. Yield affects how many functional chips emerge from the same wafer.
science.assumptions: Illustrative Poisson model with independent uniform fatal defects; real yield uses process-specific models, clustering, repair, and many nonrandom factors.

name: Copper conductor and barrier
role: Carries electrical signals and current through much of the chip wiring stack.
description: Copper wiring connects devices that would otherwise remain isolated islands. In a damascene structure, metal occupies patterned recesses in an insulating material, with barrier and liner layers separating the conductor from its surroundings. Those surrounding films are electrically significant: as a wire becomes narrower, they consume a larger fraction of its available cross section. Resistance therefore does not improve simply because the metal line becomes smaller. Material interfaces, voids, and diffusion control matter alongside copper itself. The atlas shows a cutaway conductor with its enclosure so viewers can distinguish the useful current-carrying area from the supporting films required to make that wire manufacturable and reliable.

specs.label: Role
specs.context: Used with insulating and diffusion-control films.

specs.label: Resistance trend
specs.context: Bulk geometric intuition; nanoscale effective resistivity also changes.

specs.label: Scaling concern
specs.context: A growing fraction can reduce available copper area.

tradeoff: Thinner barriers leave more copper area. Insufficient barriers can compromise dielectric and interconnect reliability.
whyAI: Moving operands is part of every AI operation. Wire resistance makes that movement consume time and energy.

sources.title: IBM Research — Copper Evolution and Beyond

scale: Nanometer-scale local lines through larger global wiring
mechanism: Form an insulating recess that defines where a wire will run.
Separate copper from surrounding material with the required interface films.
Connect the filled conductor to circuit nodes so electrical fields and current can carry signals.
misconception: A copper line is not always entirely usable copper cross section; barrier and liner films occupy part of it.

check.question: Why can a narrower copper interconnect have much higher resistance?
options: The liner becomes a superconducting shell
Its voltage is always zero
Usable copper area shrinks and nanoscale resistivity can increase
check.explanation: Geometry and material-interface effects both matter; bulk resistivity alone does not fully describe a narrow line.

science.title: Wire resistance
science.explanation: A longer line or smaller usable copper cross section increases resistance. The effective resistivity can rise at small dimensions because bulk material behavior no longer captures all scattering and interface effects.
science.assumptions: Uniform line approximation; ρ_eff must represent the actual scale and temperature. Barriers, liners, vias, and nonuniform geometry require separate treatment.

history.title: Fully integrated copper wiring demonstrated
history.significance: IBM reported integrated CMOS with multiple copper wiring levels, addressing interconnect resistance together with fabrication and reliability. This was a wiring breakthrough, not simply a smaller transistor.

source.title: Edelstein et al. — Full Copper Wiring, IEDM 1997

name: Insulators and low-k films
role: Separates conductors while shaping capacitance and electric fields.
description: A dielectric electrically separates neighboring conductors but still permits electric-field coupling. Around chip wiring, engineers seek low dielectric constant to reduce unwanted capacitance between lines. This goal differs from a transistor gate dielectric, where strong capacitive control is useful and high-k materials are employed. Some low-k films gain their properties through composition and porosity, which can make them more vulnerable to processing damage and mechanical stress. The atlas exposes the spaces between wires as functional material rather than empty background. These films help determine how much charge must move during a transition and how independently adjacent signals can operate across the integrated circuit.

specs.label: Wiring objective
specs.context: Reduce parasitic capacitance.

specs.label: Gate objective
specs.context: Increase useful capacitive control; a different application.

specs.label: Mechanical constraint
specs.context: Porosity and processing can affect robustness.

interfaces.name: Isolation
interfaces.signal: Reduced conductive leakage and controlled coupling

tradeoff: Lower k reduces coupling. Mechanical weakness and process damage can offset that electrical gain.
whyAI: Dielectrics influence the energy needed to move AI data. They also help neighboring signal paths remain reliable.

sources.title: Applied Materials — Producer Onyx and Low-k Insulation

scale: Nanometer-scale insulating films; thickness is conceptual
mechanism: Place insulating material between conductors to suppress direct conduction.
Observe that an electric field still couples neighboring conductors capacitively.
Choose material properties for the intended role: lower parasitic coupling around wires or stronger useful coupling at a gate.
misconception: High-k and low-k are not interchangeable upgrades: transistor gates and interconnect insulation pursue different capacitance goals.

check.question: Why use low-k material around signal wires?
options: To reduce unwanted capacitive coupling
To make wires intentionally conduct into one another
To increase gate control in every transistor
check.explanation: Reducing unwanted capacitance decreases the charge movement associated with transitions and coupling between neighboring lines.

science.title: Capacitive coupling
science.explanation: A larger dielectric constant or facing area increases stored charge per volt; more separation reduces this coupling. Wiring seeks to reduce this parasitic load, while gates seek strong useful control.
science.assumptions: Parallel-plate teaching model; real interconnect fields fringe in three dimensions and require field extraction.

name: Lithography and pattern transfer
role: Turns a circuit pattern into spatially selected regions on a wafer.
description: Lithography projects a patterned exposure onto a light-sensitive resist on the wafer. The developed resist then helps select where later processing changes the material; exposure alone does not deposit a complete transistor. Repeating aligned patterning steps lets many different device and wiring features meet in the intended places. Modern chipmaking uses different exposure technologies for different layers, so EUV is part of a larger manufacturing flow. Wavelength is one factor in resolution alongside optics and process methods. The atlas separates the pattern, resist, and underlying structure to show how a design acquires physical location before material processing turns that location into a functional feature.

specs.label: EUV wavelength
specs.context: Exposure wavelength; not transistor gate length.

specs.label: DUV example
specs.context: ArF exposure technology remains part of chip manufacturing.

specs.label: Critical relationship
specs.context: Features must register across repeated patterning steps.

tradeoff: Finer patterning enables denser structures. Optical complexity and process control raise manufacturing demands.
whyAI: Lithography reproduces the enormous circuit patterns needed for accelerators. Accuracy lets tiny device features connect as designed.
scale: Optical pattern transfer to nanometer-scale features
mechanism: Encode the desired spatial pattern on the lithographic mask and exposure system.
Expose and develop resist so selected regions can guide later material processing.
Align and repeat the process for additional features and layers in the circuit.
misconception: EUV’s 13.5 nm wavelength is not a measurement of a transistor gate or an entire process-node feature.

check.question: What does lithographic exposure directly create?
options: A complete working GPU
A spatial exposure pattern in resist
Every metal layer simultaneously
check.explanation: Exposure is one stage of pattern transfer. Subsequent material-processing steps create the actual device or wiring feature.

science.title: Rayleigh resolution relation
science.explanation: Critical dimension depends on exposure wavelength, numerical aperture, and a process-dependent imaging factor. This explains why wavelength, optics, and patterning methods must advance together.
science.assumptions: Lithographic scaling relation, not a direct equation for transistor gate length or a foundry node name; k₁ summarizes process and imaging choices.

history.title: Pre-production NXE:3100 EUV system ships
history.significance: The pre-production system moved 13.5 nm lithography closer to manufacturing integration. It preceded later production platforms and should not be mistaken for immediate universal EUV adoption.

source.title: ASML — Making EUV: From Lab to Fab

history.title: First NXE:3300 production EUV system ships
history.significance: ASML’s production-system shipment marked another step in the long progression from experimental exposure to manufacturing use.

source.title: ASML — Making EUV: From Lab to Fab

name: Chemical mechanical planarization
role: Restores controlled surface planarity between fabrication stages.
description: Building one patterned layer leaves topography that can interfere with the next. Chemical mechanical planarization combines chemical action with a moving pad and abrasive-containing slurry to remove excess material and control surface height. It can expose embedded features and establish a workable foundation for later processing. The process is not simply polishing the finished chip until it shines: material selectivity, remaining film thickness, and uniformity across the wafer matter. The atlas shows a partially planarized wiring surface and the desired plane, making visible why layer stacking requires repeated surface preparation. Measurement and endpoint control keep removal from erasing the structures that the preceding stages worked to create.

specs.label: Combined mechanism
specs.context: A coupled material-removal process.

specs.label: Controlled outputs
specs.context: Both local patterns and wafer-scale uniformity matter.

specs.label: Integration role
specs.context: Used at selected device and wiring stages.

tradeoff: Planarity supports the next layer. Excess removal or uneven polishing can damage existing features.
whyAI: Layered chips require controlled surfaces to remain buildable. CMP helps turn repeated fabrication steps into connected, reliable structures.

sources.title: MIT — Control of Wafer-Scale Nonuniformity in CMP

scale: Wafer-scale operation controlling nanometer-scale films
mechanism: Identify excess material and topography left by previous fabrication stages.
Use coupled chemical and mechanical action to remove material toward a controlled plane.
Measure the remaining surface and stop before critical underlying structures are damaged.
misconception: CMP is not merely cosmetic polishing after chip completion; it supports integration between selected fabrication stages.

check.question: Why is surface planarity important?
options: It makes the final chip reflective enough to compute
It eliminates the need for lithography
It prepares a controlled foundation for later layers
check.explanation: Subsequent patterning and material integration depend on controlled surface height and remaining thickness.

science.title: Preston removal relation
science.explanation: Removal rate RR is modeled using pressure P, relative sliding speed v_rel, and an empirical coefficient k_P. Chemistry, pad condition, and local pattern geometry influence the coefficient and local behavior.
science.assumptions: Empirical approximation over a calibrated regime, not a universal material law or manufacturing recipe; no process settings are prescribed.

name: Metal–oxide–semiconductor field-effect transistor
role: Uses a gate voltage to control current between source and drain.
description: The MOSFET is the central controllable device of CMOS logic. An insulated gate changes the electric potential in the semiconductor channel, regulating current between source and drain. A body or substrate is also part of the device, even when a simplified circuit symbol emphasizes only three terminals. Real operation is continuous and analog: digital circuits choose voltage ranges that stand for zero and one. The atlas cross section separates gate, dielectric, channel, terminals, and body so each function can be inspected. Its dimensions are explanatory rather than a vendor cross section. Moving outward reveals how complementary devices form gates, then memory and arithmetic, through their wiring relationships.

specs.label: Electrical terminals
specs.context: Body may be implicit in simplified diagrams.

specs.label: Control variable
specs.context: Operating behavior also depends on other terminal voltages.

specs.label: Device behavior
specs.context: Binary logic is a circuit-level abstraction.

tradeoff: Stronger drive can reduce delay. Capacitance and leakage constrain the associated power benefit.
whyAI: CMOS circuits combine these devices into digital machinery. No isolated transistor implements a neural-network concept by itself.

sources.title: MIT 6.012 — MOSFET Cross Section and Operation

scale: Nanometer-scale active features; schematic cross section
mechanism: Apply a gate voltage relative to the other transistor terminals.
Use the gate field to change the mobile charge and potential in the channel.
Allow the resulting controlled source–drain current to charge or discharge a circuit node.
misconception: A MOSFET is an analog physical device; zero and one are voltage-range conventions established by the surrounding digital circuit.

check.question: What primarily controls a MOSFET channel?
options: The gate electric field
A mechanical gate that swings open
A software token stored in the silicon atom
check.explanation: The insulated gate changes the channel’s electrostatics. Real current varies continuously with terminal voltages.

science.title: Long-channel linear-region current
science.explanation: Gate overdrive creates channel charge; drain bias drives it along the channel. Mobility, gate capacitance per area, and width-to-length ratio set the ideal current scale.
science.assumptions: Long-channel nMOS, strong inversion, 0 ≤ V_DS < V_GS − V_T, constant mobility, gradual-channel approximation; not a predictive compact model for modern short-channel FinFETs or GAA devices.

history.title: Kahng files the insulated field-effect device patent
history.significance: The patent records a controllable semiconductor device with an insulated electrode, an early foundational step toward MOS integrated circuits. The date is the filing year, not the 1963 grant year.

source.title: Kahng — US3102230A

name: Metal gate and high-k dielectric
role: Couples a control voltage into the channel while suppressing gate leakage.
description: The gate stack contains a conducting electrode separated from the semiconductor by a thin dielectric system. It controls channel charge capacitively rather than requiring intentional conduction through the gate insulator. Making traditional silicon dioxide extremely thin improved control but increased tunneling leakage. High-k materials allow a physically thicker dielectric while preserving strong electrical coupling, and metal electrodes avoid the depletion associated with older polysilicon gates. The atlas lets the gate and dielectric peel apart to make their distinct roles clear. Effective oxide thickness is an electrical comparison, not necessarily the physical thickness of the complete stack. Actual material combinations and interfaces depend on a particular manufacturing process.

specs.label: High-k example
specs.context: Commercial high-k/metal-gate introduction documented by Intel in 2007.

specs.label: Useful coupling
specs.context: Gate field controls channel charge.

specs.label: Thickness distinction
specs.context: Equivalent oxide thickness is an electrical measure.

tradeoff: Stronger coupling improves control. Leakage, interface quality, and reliability limit aggressive dielectric scaling.
whyAI: Efficient switching helps fit more operations within a power budget. Gate-stack engineering supports that hardware efficiency.

sources.title: Intel — High-k and Metal Gate Transistor Research

scale: Nanometer-scale layered stack; layers expanded for visibility
mechanism: Place a conducting gate electrode across an insulating layer from the channel.
Apply a voltage so the stack capacitively changes channel charge.
Balance useful gate coupling with tunneling leakage, interface quality, and reliability.
misconception: Equivalent oxide thickness is an electrical comparison and need not equal the physical thickness of a high-k gate stack.

check.question: Why can a high-k gate dielectric help?
options: It requires the gate to short into the channel
It can retain strong capacitive control with a physically thicker insulator
It removes every source of transistor leakage
check.explanation: Higher permittivity can preserve useful capacitance while easing the leakage problem of an extremely thin conventional dielectric.

science.title: Capacitance and equivalent oxide thickness
science.equation: C′ = ε₀ k / t; EOT ≈ t_HK (k_SiO₂ / k_HK)
science.explanation: High permittivity permits a physically thicker dielectric with comparable electrical coupling. For several dielectric layers, inverse capacitances add, so interfacial films also matter.
science.assumptions: Uniform linear dielectric layers in a series-capacitor approximation; ignores quantum capacitance and additional interface effects.

history.title: High-k and metal gates enter Intel’s 45 nm generation
history.significance: Hafnium-based dielectric and metal electrodes addressed leakage and gate-control limits of thinning silicon dioxide and polysilicon. The 45 nm name identifies the process generation.

source.title: Intel — High-k and Metal Gate Research

name: Controllable semiconductor channel
role: Forms the field-controlled conduction path inside the transistor.
description: The channel is the semiconductor region where gate voltage regulates mobile charge and conduction. In the familiar n-channel MOS teaching model, a sufficiently positive gate attracts electrons near a p-type surface and creates an inversion layer. Changing the bias changes the charge distribution rather than physically moving the source and drain together. Modern thin-body structures improve control by placing more of the channel near the gate. The atlas shows charge density as a field overlay, not a stream of independent glowing pellets whose speed equals signal propagation. Understanding the channel links the energy-band view to the transistor view: an electric field changes the conditions under which carriers can move.

specs.label: Teaching sequence
specs.context: Bias-dependent MOS surface regimes.

specs.label: Useful quantity
specs.context: Varies with terminal voltages.

specs.label: Geometry examples
specs.context: Different ways to expose the channel to gate control.

tradeoff: A thinner body improves electrostatic control. Transport, interfaces, and variability still constrain performance.
whyAI: Channel behavior sets the basic switching response. That response is multiplied across the gates executing AI workloads.
scale: Nanometer-scale active region; carrier overlay is conceptual
mechanism: Inspect the semiconductor region between the source and drain.
Change gate bias and watch the modeled mobile-charge distribution change.
Connect that charge distribution to the resulting conduction between the terminal regions.
misconception: The gate does not physically build a metal bridge; it changes carrier conditions in the semiconductor.

check.question: What changes when an inversion channel forms?
options: The source and drain move together
Silicon becomes a hollow pipe
Mobile charge near the controlled semiconductor region changes
check.explanation: The channel is controlled electrostatically. The structure remains a semiconductor device rather than a moving switch.

science.title: Inversion-sheet charge
science.explanation: For nMOS in strong inversion, the local channel potential reduces the gate overdrive available to attract mobile electron charge. The charge profile therefore changes along a biased channel.
science.assumptions: Long-channel charge-sheet approximation; Q′ is charge per area, and modern thin-body transport and quantum effects require richer models.

name: Source and drain regions
role: Connects the controlled channel to reservoirs that supply and collect carriers.
description: Source and drain are engineered semiconductor regions at the ends of the channel. They must connect efficiently to both the channel and metal contacts, making their resistance a substantial part of device design. Doping and material choice affect carrier availability, while epitaxial regions can also introduce useful strain. Advanced p-type device research includes silicon-germanium and germanium-rich approaches, but one research result should not be treated as the recipe for every commercial transistor. The atlas keeps source/drain material distinct from its metal contact. That separation explains why improving the central channel alone may deliver less benefit than expected: current still has to enter and leave through these surrounding structures.

specs.label: Electrical role
specs.context: Serve the channel through access regions.

specs.label: Engineering variables
specs.context: Process- and device-dependent.

specs.label: Resistance budget
specs.context: Separate from intrinsic channel behavior.

tradeoff: Low resistance improves drive current. Material and activation choices must remain compatible with the full device.
whyAI: Every switching event depends on carrier access. Source/drain engineering prevents that access from limiting useful compute.
scale: Nanometer-scale terminal regions; illustrative device section
mechanism: Provide terminal semiconductor regions at the two ends of the controlled channel.
Engineer carrier supply and access through material, doping, and interface choices.
Connect those regions to metal contacts and the surrounding circuit.
misconception: Source/drain regions and metal contacts are adjacent parts with different roles, not two names for the same object.

check.question: Can source/drain access limit a transistor with an excellent channel?
options: Yes; access and interface resistance remain in the current path
No; channel resistance is the only physical resistance
Only if the chip has no clock

name: Device contact and interface resistance
role: Bridges semiconductor terminals to local metallic wiring.
description: A contact connects a semiconductor region or gate electrode to the wiring above or below it. It is an interface with electrical behavior, not merely a perfect metallic plug. At a semiconductor contact, the barrier, activated dopant population, and usable area affect how readily charge can cross. Shrinking the footprint reduces area and can make contact resistance increasingly important compared with the channel resistance. The atlas exposes the junction between materials and separates contact resistance from wire resistance. Local contacts and vias may look similar in a simplified model, but contacts connect devices while vias connect wiring levels. Following this bridge leads from transistor anatomy into a complete integrated circuit.

name: Gate sidewall and inner spacers
role: Separates the gate from neighboring terminal structures and limits parasitic coupling.
description: Spacers are small dielectric structures with large integration consequences. Around the gate, they provide separation from adjacent source/drain regions and contacts. In stacked nanosheet devices, inner spacers occupy regions between sheets near the gate ends, isolating gate material from the source/drain. Their shape influences unwanted gate-to-terminal capacitance and the space available for other device features. The atlas highlights these normally overlooked volumes in a cutaway rather than hiding them behind the gate shell. This is a structural explanation, not a manufacturing recipe: forming uniform spacers requires precise material selectivity and dimensional control. Without these separators, the impressive channel geometry would not translate into the intended electrical device.

Adding fins can increase effective drive width, so the number and dimensions of fins become design choices rather than decorative repetition. The atlas compares a planar channel and fin channel at matched conceptual scale. It does not assign a modern process-node label to a measured gate length. name: Complementary CMOS inverter
role: Turns one binary voltage state into its complement.
description: A CMOS inverter joins a p-channel pull-up device to an n-channel pull-down device. Both gates receive the input; their shared output connects toward the supply for one input state and toward ground for the other. This complementary relationship restores useful signal levels and lets gates drive later gates. During a transition, the output load must charge or discharge, and the device currents change continuously. Static CMOS therefore has low ideal steady-state conduction but not zero real power consumption. The atlas exposes the two devices and the output capacitance instead of showing only a triangular symbol. This is the first place where the physical transistor becomes an explicit logical operation.

NAND is universal: networks of NAND gates can represent any Boolean function, although practical chips use many cell types for efficiency. The atlas lets a viewer trace the conducting path for each input combination. Four visible devices are enough to explain the function, while the circuit's delay still depends on physical loads and transistor choices.

For all input combinations

Internal feedback makes storage possible, while clock-controlled structures regulate when changes propagate. Data must satisfy setup and hold requirements, and the output appears after clock-to-output delay. These are physical timing constraints rather than perfectly instantaneous events. The atlas displays data, clock, and stored state separately so a viewer can watch an arithmetic result become the next stage's input. A register is a collection of such stored bits, often with additional enable and reset behavior.

The inverter pair reinforces one of two stable states while power remains applied. A word line enables access to complementary bit lines for reading or writing. Read and write circuitry around the array is essential: a lone cell does not provide a complete addressable memory. The atlas lets viewers inspect one feedback loop and then see it repeated in rows and columns with shared access wiring. This explains both the compactness of an array and the nonzero cost of moving data into and out of it. Static means no periodic refresh requirement, not permanent retention without power.

name: Full adder and carry network
role: Combines binary operands and propagates the carry needed for exact integer addition.
description: A one-bit full adder accepts two operand bits and a carry input, producing a sum bit and a carry output. Connecting these slices builds wider addition. In a ripple structure, a carry may pass through many consecutive slices before the answer settles. Faster designs compute carry relationships using additional parallel logic, trading more hardware and wiring for reduced depth. The atlas separates sum paths from carry paths so an addition becomes a visible dependency graph rather than a glowing arithmetic box. Signed interpretation, overflow, and finite output width must be specified by the surrounding architecture. The same physical logic can participate in data arithmetic, addresses, counters, and control decisions.

An array or reduction tree organizes that work; a final addition resolves the remaining result. Signed and floating-point multiplication require additional representation-specific machinery beyond this teaching example. The atlas arranges partial products in a shifted grid and highlights their reduction paths, revealing why multiplication has more structure than one isolated gate. Pipeline registers may separate stages so several products are in flight together. The shown four-bit example is deliberately small enough to inspect while preserving the dependency pattern of wider arithmetic.

That numerical distinction matters: mathematically equivalent evaluation orders need not produce identical finite-precision results. Precision, accumulation width, and throughput belong to a particular implementation and must be specified separately.

The atlas pulls the wiring layers apart while keeping their vertical vias connected, revealing how many paths cross without electrical contact. Each wire must terminate at the correct node, and its surroundings affect its signal. This hierarchy is one reason adding more arithmetic units does not guarantee proportional application speed: the units must exchange operands and results.

Clock gating can suppress unnecessary transitions in inactive blocks; separate clock and power domains support broader system management. The atlas shows the timing network independently from the data network so viewers can distinguish moving operands from the signal that schedules their capture. The clock is not a command that makes every transistor switch on each edge. Useful activity still depends on instructions, data dependencies, and available operands.

Route and verify their connections to produce a physical circuit consistent with the intended function.
misconception: A logic symbol alone is not enough to manufacture a cell; physical, electrical, timing, and process-rule information are also needed.

check.question: Which information belongs to a useful standard-cell library?
options: Only the name of the software model
Only a color for each cell
Function, timing, loading, geometry, and connection information
check.explanation: Implementation tools need both logical behavior and physical/electrical constraints to assemble a functioning chip.

science.title: Placement utilization
science.explanation: Higher utilization packs more cell area into the available region. Remaining space is useful for routing access, buffers, clock distribution, and legal placement constraints.
science.assumptions: Area bookkeeping metric; no single utilization target is optimal across process nodes or block types.

name: Streaming multiprocessor
role: Schedules many threads and supplies the execution units and nearby storage that make GPU parallelism useful.
description: An SM is a repeatable compute neighborhood inside a GPU. Instructions, thread state, arithmetic units, load/store units, registers, and local memories cooperate here. A program launches thread blocks; the GPU places eligible blocks on available SMs and divides their threads into warps. When one warp waits for data, another ready warp can make progress. This hides latency only when enough independent work and storage are available. A model layer does not correspond to one SM: its matrix tiles are distributed across many SMs, and the same hardware is reused for later layers. The atlas separates scheduling, execution, and storage to show why adding arithmetic alone cannot guarantee a faster model.

specs.label: Warp width
specs.context: CUDA execution grouping, not 32 entire model requests.

specs.label: Resident warps
specs.context: Blackwell compute capability 10.0; occupancy also depends on resource use.

specs.label: Resident blocks
specs.context: Blackwell 10.0 architectural limit, not a promised active count.

tradeoff: More resident work can hide latency, but each block consumes finite registers and shared memory. Maximum occupancy can be slower than a carefully tiled kernel with fewer active blocks.
whyAI: Transformer layers become thousands of tile operations scheduled across these neighborhoods. The SM is where software parallelism becomes simultaneous transistor activity.
scale: Conceptual region of a centimeter-scale die; schematic floorplan
mechanism: A kernel launch creates a grid of thread blocks; the GPU places blocks on SMs where enough registers and shared memory are available.
Each block is divided into warps, and schedulers select ready instructions to feed arithmetic, tensor, or load/store pipelines.
Completed tiles are written or passed onward; the same SM then processes additional tiles and later model layers.
misconception: A model layer is not a dedicated physical layer of GPU silicon. Many SMs process pieces of one layer, then reuse the same circuits for the next.

check.question: Why can a kernel with more arithmetic units still spend time waiting?
options: It must wait for enough operands or independent ready work.
An SM can execute only one complete neural-network layer per second.
Registers permanently store all the model weights.
check.explanation: Arithmetic units are useful only when instructions and data are ready. Memory latency and resource limits can leave execution capacity idle.

science.title: Compute and data supply must balance
science.explanation: P is throughput in operations per second, B is useful memory bandwidth in bytes per second, and I is arithmetic intensity in operations per byte moved at the chosen memory level. The sloped region is limited by operand delivery; the horizontal region is limited by arithmetic throughput. Tiling can raise I without changing the model by reusing a value several times after one load.
science.assumptions: An upper-bound roofline model for a stated operation type and memory level. It excludes launch latency, dependency stalls, occupancy limits, and communication outside that level; peaks must use the same precision and sparsity convention.

history.title: CUDA opens GPU execution to general computation
history.significance: NVIDIA introduced the CUDA architecture in 2006, allowing computational workloads to use GPU throughput without expressing the problem through graphics APIs. A programmable parallel hierarchy gave researchers a practical path from scientific and numerical code to large numbers of GPU execution units.

name: Tensor Core matrix unit
role: Multiplies small matrix tiles and accumulates their products with supported numerical formats.
description: A Tensor Core implements matrix multiply and accumulate: D equals A times B plus C. It does not contain a neural network, words, or a complete attention head. Software divides larger tensors into compatible tiles, arranges their layout, and feeds these units repeatedly. Different instructions accept different input formats and accumulation rules. Low precision reduces the bits moved and processed, while scale factors help represent useful numerical ranges. A peak throughput figure assumes suitable operations, shapes, clocks, and a continuous supply of operands. The visualization should show a row meeting a column, partial products accumulating, and the resulting tile joining a larger matrix. This makes the arithmetic visible without pretending the rendered grid is a literal chip photograph.

specs.context: Matrix multiply-accumulate, or MMA.

specs.label: Generation
specs.context: Datacenter Blackwell; supported instruction details depend on architecture target.

specs.label: NVFP4 pair peak
specs.context: Official GB200 Superchip table: two GPUs, theoretical tensor peak.

interfaces.signal: A and B tiles plus scale metadata

tradeoff: Lower precision can raise throughput and reduce memory traffic, but numerical error must be controlled. Sparse peak rates require the supported sparsity pattern and cannot be applied to arbitrary dense weights.
whyAI: Attention projections and feed-forward layers are dominated by matrix products. Efficient tensor kernels turn this recurring mathematical structure into much more work per joule.
scale: Subregion of an SM; logical matrix tiles enlarged for inspection
mechanism: Software divides a large matrix product into compatible tiles and selects a supported input format, layout, and scaling scheme.
The tensor instruction multiplies corresponding tile elements and accumulates partial sums according to its numerical rules.
Partial tiles are combined or reused, then written into the larger output tensor for the next operation.
misconception: Tensor Core sparse peak performance is not a dense-model guarantee. The supported sparsity pattern and appropriate instructions are required to realize the sparse rating.

check.question: What does a Tensor Core primarily accelerate?
options: Storing model files after power is removed.
Matrix multiply-accumulate operations on compatible tiles.
Replacing the CPU operating system.
check.explanation: Neural-network projections are built from large matrix products. Tensor Cores accelerate small pieces of those products, which software assembles into the complete result.

science.title: Why matrix size and reuse matter
science.explanation: A has m rows and k columns; B has k rows and n columns. Their product needs approximately mnk fused multiply-adds, conventionally counted as two floating-point operations each. If all elements occupy b bytes, the denominator describes reading A and B once and writing the output once. Increasing reuse can make compute grow faster than external data movement.
science.assumptions: Ideal dense C = AB traffic, with each matrix transferred once and no initial C read. Accumulation precision can differ in real kernels; a D = AB + C operation must include its extra C traffic. This is an arithmetic model, not measured Tensor Core efficiency.

history.title: Volta introduces NVIDIA Tensor Cores
history.significance: NVIDIA announced Volta and Tesla V100 on May 10, 2017. Dedicated Tensor Cores accelerated matrix arithmetic, aligning silicon execution more directly with the multiply-and-accumulate structure of deep learning instead of relying only on general-purpose arithmetic lanes.

name: Register file
role: Keeps each active thread’s immediate values close to the arithmetic pipelines.
description: Registers hold the addresses, counters, partial results, and scalar operands that threads need immediately. The compiler assigns program values to a finite physical pool. A value in a register does not need a fresh trip to off-chip memory for every instruction. If a kernel asks for too many registers, fewer blocks may fit at once; some values may also spill into local memory, which is backed by device memory and cached. Registers are private to a thread in the programming model, although explicit warp shuffle instructions can exchange values between participating threads. The atlas should depict narrow banks feeding arithmetic lanes, then contrast a short local reuse loop with the longer path caused by a spill.

specs.label: Pool per SM
specs.context: Blackwell architectural register-file count.

specs.label: Per-thread limit
specs.context: Architectural maximum; allocation granularity and occupancy also matter.

specs.label: Warp exchange
specs.context: Explicit register-value exchange among participating warp threads.

interfaces.name: Spill path
interfaces.signal: Values moved to device-backed local memory

tradeoff: Keeping more intermediates in registers can reduce traffic, but large allocations limit parallel residency. Kernel fusion therefore needs a balance between reuse and register pressure.
whyAI: Matrix kernels, normalization, and attention all reuse small values many times. Register allocation can change their speed even when the mathematical model remains identical.

sources.title: NVIDIA: Register Cache for Warp-Centric CUDA Programs

scale: On-die storage banks; physical bank dimensions are schematic
mechanism: The compiler maps frequently used thread values to registers, subject to the available register pool and allocation rules.
Execution pipelines repeatedly read and update those nearby values without fetching them anew from HBM.
If register demands exceed a useful allocation, parallel residency can fall or values can spill to device-backed local memory.
misconception: CUDA local memory does not mean physically nearest to a thread. Register spills to local memory are backed by device memory and may be cached.

check.question: What can happen when each thread uses many more registers?
options: The GPU gains more physical register capacity automatically.
The model becomes permanently stored on the die.
Fewer blocks fit concurrently, or some values spill.
check.explanation: Registers are a finite resource shared among resident work. More per-thread state can trade local reuse for lower concurrency or extra memory traffic.

science.title: Register allocation limits resident work
science.explanation: RSM is the number of available 32-bit registers per SM, rthread is registers requested per thread, and Tblock is threads per block. Their product estimates the register footprint of one block. Doubling the per-thread requirement can reduce the number of blocks that fit, even though it may save loads by retaining more intermediate results.
science.assumptions: A register-only upper bound, assuming uniform allocation. Hardware allocation granularity, reserved resources, warp/block limits, and shared-memory use can lower residency further. It is not a complete CUDA occupancy calculator.

name: Shared memory SRAM
role: Lets cooperating threads explicitly stage and reuse a tile near the compute units.
description: Shared memory is a software-managed scratchpad allocated to a thread block. Threads cooperate to load a tile, synchronize when required, and reuse it for several operations before replacing it. Its underlying storage is SRAM, which retains state while powered without the periodic refresh needed by DRAM. Shared memory is banked, so the access pattern matters: requests to different words in the same bank can serialize. Padding or rearranging a tile can remove those conflicts. The capacity is small compared with HBM, but a small tile can be reused many times. The visual should expose a banked array with a selectable conflict pattern, showing why an extra column of padding can accelerate an otherwise unchanged matrix transpose.

specs.label: Address banks
specs.context: Successive 32-bit words map to successive banks in CUDA shared memory.

specs.label: Capacity per SM
specs.context: Blackwell compute capability 10.0 shared-memory carveout.

specs.label: Per-block maximum
specs.context: One KB reserved by CUDA; dynamic opt-in required above static limits.

interfaces.name: Synchronization
interfaces.signal: Barriers establishing when staged data are ready

tradeoff: Larger tiles improve reuse but consume more scratchpad and may reduce active blocks. Bank conflicts can waste this fast storage unless the layout matches the access pattern.
whyAI: Attention kernels can avoid materializing large intermediate matrices in HBM by combining local tiles with online reductions. The savings come from a better dataflow, not extra model parameters.
scale: On-die SRAM banks; logical address map rather than transistor layout
mechanism: Cooperating threads or a copy engine bring a reusable tile from device memory into a block’s shared-memory allocation.
A synchronization point establishes readiness; threads then read the tile repeatedly while computing several outputs.
The block reuses the scratchpad for another tile, choosing an address layout that avoids conflicting accesses to the same bank.
misconception: Shared memory and L1 cache are not interchangeable programming concepts. Shared memory is explicitly managed by software; cache retention is automatic.

check.question: Why might adding one padding column to a shared-memory tile improve performance?
options: It increases HBM capacity.
It can redirect accesses across different banks and avoid serialization.
It adds more Tensor Cores to the SM.
check.explanation: Padding changes address-to-bank mapping. The arithmetic can stay identical while the memory requests stop competing for the same bank.

science.title: Address layout determines bank conflicts
science.explanation: a is a byte address for a 32-bit word in the documented shared-memory organization. Adjacent words land in different banks, while addresses separated by 128 bytes return to the same bank. A warp accessing different words in one bank may serialize. Padding a two-dimensional array changes its row stride and can transform a column access from conflicting to distributed.
science.assumptions: 32 banks and 4-byte word mapping in the referenced CUDA programming model. Wider instructions may be split into transactions; broadcast of the same read address is a special case and is not equivalent to different-word conflicts.

name: L1 and texture cache
role: Automatically retains recently accessed data and combines nearby thread requests near an SM.
description: The L1 cache is the first automatic cache close to an SM’s execution units. When threads request memory, hardware checks whether useful data are already nearby. Hits can avoid a longer journey; misses continue toward lower levels of the hierarchy. Consecutive thread addresses can be coalesced into fewer memory transactions, while scattered addresses may move many unused bytes. Blackwell shares a physical capacity budget among L1, texture functionality, and the shared-memory carveout. This differs from the explicit ownership and lifetime of software-managed shared memory. The atlas should trace the same load with a hit and a miss, then reveal how reshaping a warp’s addresses changes traffic without changing the values the program computes.

specs.label: Combined capacity
specs.context: Blackwell B200 L1/texture/shared-memory aggregate; not 256 KB of L1 plus shared memory.

specs.label: Allocation
specs.context: A larger shared-memory reservation leaves a different cache allocation.

specs.label: Coalescing example
specs.context: CUDA programming guidance; actual request handling depends on instruction and access pattern.

interfaces.name: Cache miss
interfaces.signal: Request toward L2 and device memory

tradeoff: A cache helps when nearby or recent data will be reused, but unpredictable access can defeat locality. Increasing software-managed shared memory can improve explicit reuse while reducing space available to automatic caching.
whyAI: Embedding lookups, normalization, and intermediate tensor access can become memory limited. Data layout determines whether the hierarchy moves useful numbers or mostly unused bytes.

sources.title: NVIDIA CUDA C++ Best Practices Guide

scale: On-die memory near SMs; illustrative cache lines
mechanism: Threads issue addresses, and the memory system combines compatible nearby requests into transactions.
A cache lookup supplies data that are already present near the SM; a miss continues toward the next memory level.
Returned data may populate the cache, making later local or nearby accesses less expensive.
misconception: A 256 KB combined L1/texture/shared-memory capacity does not mean 256 KB of L1 plus another 256 KB of shared memory. They share a capacity budget.

check.question: Which access pattern generally makes better use of memory transactions?
options: Nearby threads requesting neighboring useful values.
Every thread requesting an unrelated distant address.
Every load deliberately bypassing all reuse.
check.explanation: Coalescing can serve neighboring addresses with fewer transactions, reducing the number of unused bytes moved for the same computation.

science.title: Useful bytes versus bytes actually moved
science.equation: ηuseful = Museful / Mtransferred; Buseful = ηuseful × Btransferred
science.explanation: Museful counts bytes the computation needs; Mtransferred counts all bytes fetched in the memory transactions serving those needs. A scattered access pattern can move many unused bytes, reducing effective bandwidth even if the physical interface is busy. Coalescing neighboring thread requests and reusing cache lines improve the fraction of movement that performs useful work.
science.assumptions: Accounting over the same interval and memory boundary. Count unique or repeated demand consistently, and treat compression, cache hits, write traffic, and replayed transactions separately when profiling.

name: Shared L2 cache
role: Provides a larger on-chip reuse layer between SM traffic and HBM.
description: L2 sits farther from individual execution units and serves requests across the GPU. A tile loaded by one part of the chip can remain available for later work, reducing traffic to external HBM. The cache is physically distributed even when software sees one device address space. Address placement and work placement can therefore influence the distance data travels. Persistence controls can help protect selected reuse, but they do not make the entire model fit into cache. A useful view shows multiple SMs converging on cache slices, with a counter for bytes served locally versus bytes fetched from HBM. Cache capacity should be compared with a working set, not confused with total model storage.

specs.label: Published capacity
specs.context: NVIDIA Blackwell Tuning Guide labels this as GB200 GPU L2 capacity.

specs.label: Scope
specs.context: Physically distributed; not private storage for each SM.

specs.label: Reuse control
specs.context: CUDA policies influence retention; they are not capacity guarantees.

interfaces.name: Cache response
interfaces.signal: Reused data to requesting compute units

tradeoff: A larger cache can save external bandwidth but consumes expensive logic-die area. Locality and scheduling can matter as much as nominal capacity when requests cross internal partitions.
whyAI: Reused weights and intermediate tensors can be served without another HBM access. This helps only when the active working set and access pattern fit the cache hierarchy.

sources.title: NVIDIA: GPU locality domains and L2 fabric
MIT Computation Structures: cache hierarchy and average access time

scale: Distributed banks across a centimeter-scale GPU die
mechanism: Requests that cannot be satisfied close to an SM reach shared L2 cache slices through the internal fabric.
An L2 hit returns retained data; a miss asks the memory controllers to fetch data from HBM.
Reuse by later work can avoid additional HBM trips, while replacement policies and working-set size determine what remains available.
misconception: A unified device address space does not mean every physical memory route has identical cost. Distributed cache and internal locality can still matter.

check.question: When does a larger L2 cache most directly help?
options: Whenever a model has more vocabulary entries, regardless of access.
Only when the network cable is unplugged.
When useful data are reused before they are evicted.
check.explanation: A cache reduces external traffic when it retains data that will be needed again. Capacity alone does not create reuse.

science.title: Average access cost across two cache levels
science.explanation: tL1 and tL2 are lookup times; mL1 is the fraction missing in L1 and mL2 is the fraction of those requests that also miss in L2. tHBM is the additional service time after an L2 miss. Lowering mL2 prevents some expensive trips to HBM, making a cache useful even when it stores only a small portion of total device memory.
science.assumptions: A sequential lookup model with conditional miss rates and incremental latency terms. Real GPUs overlap requests, queue transactions, and hide latency with other work, so AMAT is not the same as kernel execution time.

name: On-chip interconnect fabric
role: Routes data and control between compute units, cache slices, memory controllers, and I/O.
description: The on-chip fabric is the communication system within the silicon. Requests carry addresses, operation types, and data between blocks; arbitration decides which request uses a contested path. Wires have capacitance and resistance, so longer journeys consume time and energy even before leaving the package. A GPU can expose a unified address space while still having internal locality domains. The atlas should distinguish an illustrative routing graph from an undisclosed physical topology: a tidy mesh is a teaching model, not a claim that Blackwell uses that exact network. Animate contention at shared routes and show local versus remote cache access, making it clear that the chip is a coordinated system rather than an undifferentiated slab of arithmetic.

specs.label: Endpoints
specs.context: Logical component classes; exact proprietary topology is not asserted.

specs.label: Address view
specs.context: Physical locality can still affect movement cost.

specs.label: Constraint
specs.context: No unsupported numerical internal-fabric rating is assigned.

interfaces.name: Request injection
interfaces.signal: Addressed transactions from compute or I/O

interfaces.name: Routing
interfaces.signal: Packets or transactions to selected internal endpoints

tradeoff: Wider routes and more buffering improve communication capacity but consume area and power. Placing related work and data near one another can reduce movement before any hardware is added.
whyAI: Thousands of concurrent tensor operations must obtain operands and exchange results. Internal communication determines whether the advertised arithmetic units remain busy.

scale: Millimeter-to-centimeter internal routes; illustrative topology
mechanism: A compute, cache, or I/O block injects an addressed transaction into the chip’s communication fabric.
Routing and arbitration carry that transaction toward its destination while managing competition and backpressure.
The response returns through the fabric; repeated or long-distance traffic consumes bandwidth, energy, and time.
misconception: The atlas’s routing graph is a teaching diagram, not a verified Blackwell mesh layout. A physical topology should not be inferred from the illustrative geometry.

check.question: Why does locality still matter inside one GPU?
options: Only data outside the rack require energy to move.
Internal wires and shared routes still incur delay, energy, and contention.
One GPU contains only one possible data route.
check.explanation: Even on one chip, communication has physical costs. Keeping related data and work nearby can reduce unnecessary traffic.

science.title: Enough requests must be in flight
science.equation: Ninflight = λ × L; Minflight ≈ B × L
science.explanation: Little’s law relates average in-flight request count N to completed requests per second λ and average request latency L. Multiplying byte throughput B by latency gives the corresponding amount of in-flight data. A fabric can have wide links yet remain underused if the workload or queues cannot sustain enough independent transactions to cover the round trip.
science.assumptions: Stable steady-state averages with the same system boundary for arrivals, completions, and latency. The byte form assumes consistent payload accounting. It supplies a concurrency requirement, not a claim about Blackwell’s undisclosed queue depths.

name: HBM controller and PHY
role: Schedules DRAM commands and translates on-chip requests into the electrical signals of the memory interface.
description: A memory controller turns requests for addresses into commands that the DRAM organization can execute. It coordinates reads, writes, timing constraints, and maintenance such as refresh. The PHY is the physical interface circuitry that drives and receives signals across package wires. These are distinct jobs: the controller manages the protocol and schedule, while the PHY makes the bits electrically reliable. Many parallel wires provide aggregate HBM bandwidth without demanding that each wire run at the highest possible rate. The atlas should expose queues, bank selection, and read responses, then follow them across the interposer into the stacked memory. Published stack bandwidth is an upper-bound interface capability, not the sustained bandwidth of every access pattern.

specs.label: HBM3E interface width
specs.context: HBM3E wide-interface organization; excludes command, clock, power, and ground connections.

specs.label: Reference GPU memory bandwidth
specs.context: Derived from the GB200 product table’s 16 TB/s per two-GPU Superchip.

specs.label: Memory access
specs.context: Protocol scheduling and physical signaling are separate functions.

tradeoff: Wider interfaces increase bandwidth but require dense package routing and more connections. Poorly localized or conflicting accesses can achieve much less than the aggregate peak.
whyAI: Decoding a token often streams many model weights, so memory delivery can dominate latency. HBM controllers connect large model state to the much smaller arithmetic neighborhoods.

sources.title: Intel: Memory performance, latency, and bandwidth
John D. C. Little (1961): A Proof for the Queuing Formula L = λW

scale: Die-edge interface blocks and millimeter package links; schematic layout
mechanism: The controller accepts memory requests, maps addresses to memory resources, and schedules legal operations around timing constraints.
The PHY drives or receives many electrical signals across the package interface to the selected HBM stack.
Read data return to the cache and fabric, while refresh and other maintenance continue alongside application traffic.
misconception: Rated aggregate HBM bandwidth is not the speed of every individual access. Bank conflicts, transfer patterns, and protocol timing affect sustained throughput.

check.question: What is the difference between the controller and the PHY?
options: The controller schedules memory operations; the PHY implements electrical signaling.
The controller stores all weights; the PHY performs attention.
They are two names for an NVMe drive.
check.explanation: Protocol scheduling and physical bit transmission are distinct functions, even when integrated into one memory-interface subsystem.

science.title: Concurrent requests cover memory latency
science.explanation: Btarget is the desired useful bandwidth in bytes per second, L is average request latency in seconds, and s is useful bytes per completed request. The result estimates how many independent requests must be outstanding. Sequentially dependent loads may fail to expose that concurrency even when the memory stack advertises ample bandwidth; controller queues cannot create independence absent from the program.
science.assumptions: Steady-state Little’s-law estimate with a consistent request size and measured latency. Bank timing, refresh, arbitration, and protocol overhead determine the achievable B and L; no vendor queue capacity is assumed.

name: NVLink GPU interface
role: Moves tensor data between GPUs through a high-bandwidth scale-up interconnect.
description: A model can be partitioned across GPUs because one device may not provide enough memory or enough compute. NVLink supplies a fast path for those devices to exchange tensor pieces and partial results. Physical links connect GPUs to peers or switches; software still chooses a parallel strategy and schedules the required communication. A connected group is not automatically one ordinary GPU with uniform access costs. Collective operations, message size, synchronization, and topology all affect useful performance. The atlas should show a tensor being divided, processed, and reduced across devices, with communication time visible alongside arithmetic. NVLink is distinct from the internal die-to-die interface and from the network that joins racks.

specs.label: Blackwell NVLink 5
specs.context: Aggregate across 18 links; both directions summed.

specs.label: Link count
specs.context: 100 GB/s bidirectional per link in NVIDIA’s specification.

specs.label: NVL72 aggregation
specs.context: Rack aggregate interface bandwidth; not the bandwidth of one transfer.

interfaces.signal: Tensor partitions, reductions, and peer memory traffic

whyAI: Tensor and expert parallelism depend on exchanging activations or partial sums between accelerators. Scale-up communication lets nearby GPUs cooperate more efficiently on one model.

NVLink-connected endpoints transfer those buffers through the supported peer or switched fabric.
Collective operations combine or distribute the results, then dependent computation proceeds when the required data are ready.

options: Refreshing a single DRAM capacitor.
Encoding a text token into its vocabulary ID.
Exchanging tensors among GPUs in a scale-up domain.

science.title: Communication has volume and startup costs
science.explanation: p is the number of ranks, M is each rank’s input size in bytes, α is startup time per ring step, and β is effective one-direction payload bandwidth per rank. name: Tensor Memory
role: Provides dedicated on-chip storage for fifth-generation Tensor Core operands and accumulators.
description: Tensor Memory is a Blackwell storage space specialized for Tensor Core operations. It is neither HBM nor the Tensor Memory Accelerator. Supported instructions allocate columns, move suitable fragments, launch matrix operations, and later retrieve results. Giving tensor operations their own storage changes how software pipelines matrix multiplication and manages register pressure. The programming model has explicit access and allocation rules, so the whole array is not a freely interchangeable replacement for ordinary shared memory. The atlas can reveal a matrix-shaped store next to the Tensor Core, highlight allocated columns, and show accumulators staying nearby through several operations. Label this an architectural address layout rather than a literal photograph of the physical memory cells.

specs.context: Total logical array is 256 KiB by direct multiplication.

whyAI: Large matrix products repeatedly update partial sums before storing final values. Keeping these accumulators next to the tensor machinery improves the opportunity for reuse.

mechanism: A supported kernel allocates columns in Tensor Memory and arranges tensor fragments according to the instruction’s required layout.
Tensor Core operations consume operands and update accumulators using this specialized nearby storage.
The kernel synchronizes, extracts completed results through supported instructions, and releases the allocation when it is no longer needed.

Holding specialized Tensor Core operands and accumulators on the chip.
Routing Ethernet packets between racks.

science.title: Logical shape determines storage capacity
science.explanation: The documented sm_100a/sm_100f address view has 128 rows, 512 columns, and 32 bits per cell. Dividing bits by eight gives bytes. This organization explains why column allocation reserves an entire vertical set of cells and why instruction layouts govern access. The number describes the architectural array, not a claim that every simultaneously resident block can consume an independent full-size copy.

name: Tensor Memory Accelerator
role: Moves multidimensional tensor tiles asynchronously so compute threads can spend less effort copying data.
description: TMA is a data movement engine. Software describes a tensor and its layout, then requests transfers while other work proceeds. This reduces the need for threads to compute every address and issue every individual load during tile staging. The result is not instantaneous memory: the transfer still uses bandwidth, must complete, and needs the correct synchronization before consumers use its data. Pipelines can stage the next tile while the current tile is being multiplied. First introduced with Hopper and extended on Blackwell, this mechanism is separate from Blackwell Tensor Memory, which stores tensor operands and accumulators. The atlas should make the copy engine and its destination buffer separate objects, joined by an animated completion signal.

whyAI: Transformer kernels repeatedly stage blocks of weights and activations. A copy engine frees execution resources and makes sustained matrix throughput easier to approach.
