check.question: How does a pipelined kernel benefit from TMA?
options: It can prepare a future tile while computing on the current tile.
It eliminates the need for HBM or shared memory.
It makes every model use the same matrix dimensions.
check.explanation: The gain comes from overlapping movement and computation and reducing thread work spent on copying, subject to bandwidth and buffering limits.

science.title: Overlap changes a sum into a bottleneck
science.explanation: N is the number of equal tiles. After filling the first stage, a two-stage pipeline can load the next tile while computing on the current one. The slower stage sets the steady-state cadence. Without overlap, the same sequence takes approximately N × (tload + tcompute), so copy/compute overlap can improve throughput without increasing the arithmetic rate.
science.assumptions: Ideal independent load and compute resources, adequate double buffering, equal tile times, and negligible synchronization overhead. Shared bandwidth or resource contention can reduce or remove overlap. TMA remains a copy engine, distinct from Tensor Memory storage.

history.title: Hopper introduces Tensor Memory Accelerator

name: GPU logic dies
role: Integrate transistor circuits into the compute, storage, and communication structures of one accelerator.
description: A logic die is a piece cut from a processed silicon wafer. Its surface carries layers of transistors and metal interconnect that implement arithmetic, memories, control, and interfaces. Datacenter Blackwell combines two large logic dies into one GPU, crossing the boundary with a dedicated high-bandwidth interface. This permits more circuitry than one exposure-sized die while preserving a single accelerator programming view. The package must connect those dies to each other, to memory stacks, and to power and cooling structures. In the exploded view, show functional regions without presenting their proportions as a verified proprietary floorplan. The two dies should reconnect through many short parallel routes, illustrating why packaging is part of the architecture rather than merely a protective box.

To avoid needing any package wiring.
To integrate more circuitry than one exposure-sized logic die can provide.

science.title: Switching activity becomes heat
science.explanation: α is the average charging activity per clock, Cswitched is effective switched capacitance, V is supply voltage, and f is clock frequency. Raising voltage has a quadratic effect in this model, while raising frequency has a linear effect. Consequently, adding transistors or increasing clocks does not provide free computation; energy-efficient architecture also reduces moved capacitance and unnecessary switching.
science.assumptions: First-order CMOS capacitive switching model. Leakage, short-circuit current, clock networks, memory, I/O, and conversion losses contribute additional power; voltage and frequency are not independent across valid operating points. No Blackwell rail value is inferred.

name: High-bandwidth memory stack
role: Stacks DRAM vertically beside the processor to provide large capacity through a very wide local interface.
description: An HBM stack places several thin DRAM dies above a base interface and connects them vertically. It stores model weights, activations, optimizer state, and attention caches while the system is powered. The stack sits near the GPU on an advanced package, shortening the routes for a broad parallel interface. More layers generally add capacity; bandwidth also depends on interface width and per-pin transfer rate, so doubling stack height does not automatically double bandwidth. The atlas should explode one stack into its DRAM layers, then reconnect it through vertical vias and package wiring to the processor. Capacity, interface bandwidth, and the system’s exposed usable memory should remain separate readouts because they describe different parts of the product.

mechanism: Multiple thin DRAM dies are stacked and connected vertically to form a compact memory assembly.
The stack connects to the GPU through a wide package interface that transfers many bits in parallel.
The controller repeatedly reads and writes model state while refresh preserves the volatile DRAM contents.
misconception: Increasing the number of stacked DRAM layers primarily adds capacity. Bandwidth also depends on interface width and operating rate, so it does not automatically scale with height.

check.question: What mainly distinguishes HBM’s approach from simply raising the speed of a narrow memory bus?
options: HBM eliminates all DRAM refresh operations.
It uses many parallel data connections close to the processor.
It stores bits permanently without electrical power.
check.explanation: A very wide nearby interface provides high aggregate bandwidth. Stacking adds capacity in a compact footprint, while the memory remains volatile.

science.title: Parallel width creates aggregate bandwidth
science.explanation: Wdata is the number of active data wires and rpin is the transfer rate in bits per second on each wire. The factor eight converts bits into bytes. Stacking more DRAM layers increases storage capacity, whereas interface width and signaling rate determine this bandwidth ceiling. These are separate design dimensions, explaining why a taller memory stack need not be a faster one.
science.assumptions: Ideal interface payload rate before command, refresh, bank-conflict, or scheduling losses. Count only data wires, and use a rate definition consistent with the signaling format. Capacity and bandwidth refer to a named stack configuration.

name: DRAM die and memory banks
role: Stores dense arrays of charge-based bits and organizes them into banks for read, write, and refresh.
description: A DRAM die is mostly an organized landscape of memory cells. In the common one-transistor, one-capacitor cell, stored charge represents a bit and the transistor controls access to it. Word lines select rows; bit lines carry the small electrical changes that sense amplifiers detect and restore. The charge leaks, so refresh is part of normal operation. Banks provide opportunities for overlapping work, but timing constraints mean that an arbitrary stream of addresses does not behave like one continuous pipe. The atlas should descend from a memory bank into a row and finally one cell, then pull back to show how billions of these tiny storage sites become the weight and activation tensors visible to software.

whyAI: Billions of model parameters are ultimately stored as physical bit patterns. DRAM supplies the capacity that small on-chip SRAM structures cannot economically provide.

mechanism: A selected word line enables access transistors, coupling the chosen memory cells to their bit lines.
Sense amplifiers detect and restore small charge-dependent signals so reads produce reliable digital values.
Refresh revisits stored rows before leakage destroys their contents, while banks schedule application accesses around maintenance.

check.question: Why does conventional DRAM need refresh?
options: Stored capacitor charge gradually leaks away.
Every memory cell is an optical fiber.
Refresh downloads a new model from the network.
check.explanation: Charge-based storage is compact but not indefinitely stable. Periodic restoration keeps the bit values intact while power is available.

science.title: A stored bit begins as a tiny voltage perturbation
science.explanation: When the access transistor connects a selected cell to a precharged bit line, their capacitances share charge. Because the bit line can be much larger than the cell capacitance, the initial voltage change is small. A sense amplifier must detect its sign and restore a full logic level, connecting the microscopic capacitor directly to the digital bit used by software.
science.assumptions: Ideal charge sharing before amplification, with fixed capacitances and no leakage, access resistance, coupling noise, or transistor threshold effects. Actual DRAM sensing and retention require a full circuit model.

history.title: Dennard’s DRAM cell patent is granted
history.significance: Robert Dennard’s field-effect memory patent, filed in 1967 after his 1966 work at IBM, was granted on June 4, 1968. A compact access device and charge-storage element established the basis for dense dynamic memory, with periodic restoration as part of normal operation.

name: Through-silicon via
role: Provides a vertical electrical connection through silicon between stacked layers.
description: A TSV is a conductive route that passes through the thickness of silicon. In a memory stack, many such routes provide data, control, and power connections between levels and the base. This avoids forcing all communication around the outside edge of each die. The via needs electrical isolation from the surrounding silicon, and its processing must coexist with the circuits and mechanical stresses of thin dies. A TSV is not itself a memory bit and should not be drawn as a data storage column. The cutaway should show a conductor, surrounding insulation, and nearby circuitry, then zoom out to many repeated connections. Connections between surfaces still require bonding structures, so TSVs and microbumps are related but distinct parts.

mechanism: A via structure is formed through silicon, with insulation separating its conductor from the surrounding material.

Many vias carry signals and supplies vertically, joining stacked circuits into a connected memory structure.
misconception: A TSV is a vertical connection, not a column of stored memory bits. The DRAM cells storing those bits are separate circuits beside the interconnect.

options: Only the server to a distant data center.
Only photons inside a laser.
Electrical structures across the thickness of a silicon die.
check.explanation: Through-silicon vias provide vertical electrical routes, which are especially useful when several memory dies are stacked.

science.title: Via geometry affects electrical resistance
science.explanation: ρ is conductor resistivity, ℓ is via length, and r is conductor radius. A shorter or wider conductor lowers its DC resistance. This benefit competes with the silicon area and stress region consumed by the via. Many parallel vertical connections therefore require both electrical design and mechanical/process integration, rather than merely drilling the maximum number of holes.
science.assumptions: A uniform cylindrical conductor in the ohmic, low-frequency regime. Contact resistance, barrier layers, temperature, skin effects, and size-dependent resistivity are omitted. The equation supplies no proprietary TSV dimensions.

name: Interposer and redistribution layers
role: Connects logic dies and memory through dense package-level wiring.
description: The interposer is the wiring platform between fine-pitch die connections and the larger package substrate. It lets a GPU sit close to several memory stacks with many parallel connections. Advanced packaging does not always use a single uniform slab of silicon: TSMC’s CoWoS family includes silicon interposers, redistribution-layer approaches, and local silicon interconnects embedded where higher connection density is needed. The atlas should let viewers peel back the layers and trace one GPU-to-HBM route. It should label the generic construction being shown and avoid assigning an exact unpublished package cross-section to a named accelerator. Dense local wiring makes the package function like a small system assembled from dies optimized for different jobs.

mechanism: Fine-pitch terminals from logic and memory land on the dense interconnect platform.

check.question: What is the interposer’s central contribution to an AI accelerator?
options: It executes the operating system.
It provides dense local routing between logic dies and memory.
It replaces all cooling equipment.
check.explanation: High-bandwidth memory needs a large number of nearby connections to the processor. Dense package routing makes those connections physically practical.

science.title: Long resistive routes can become disproportionately slow
science.explanation: R′ and C′ are resistance and capacitance per unit length; ℓ is route length. In a distributed RC approximation, doubling a comparable unbuffered route can increase its delay by about four times. Dense package integration shortens routes between logic and memory and can reduce capacitance as well as physical distance, helping explain its performance and energy value.
science.assumptions: RC-dominated, uniform unbuffered interconnect with fixed cross-section and loading convention. High-speed package channels can require transmission-line and full electromagnetic models; the proportionality is not a measured interposer delay specification.

name: Microbumps and bonding joints
role: Join matching electrical terminals at the surfaces of dies and package interconnect layers.
description: Microbumps are small conductive joints arranged in dense arrays. They connect one surface to another, such as a die to an interposer or adjacent memory layers. The surrounding underfill helps support the assembly and manage stress from materials expanding differently with temperature. A bump is a connection, while a TSV is a route through silicon; the two can meet but should not be drawn as the same object. Finer pitch supports more connections in a given area, yet raises demands on alignment, planarity, cleanliness, and defect control. The atlas should separate two mating surfaces, reveal the array of joints, and animate one signal crossing the interface before the package closes again.

mechanism: Matching terminals are formed on the surfaces that will be joined, using a connection pitch appropriate to the package process.
Alignment and bonding create conductive joints between the surfaces.
Underfill and surrounding structures support the joint array as the assembly heats, cools, and experiences mechanical stress.

check.question: Why is a finer bump pitch useful?
options: It fits more electrical connections into a given surface area.
It removes the need to align the surfaces.
It directly increases the number of software model layers.
check.explanation: Connection density enables wider interfaces and more integration, but finer spacing also tightens manufacturing tolerances.

science.title: Pitch controls the connection budget
science.explanation: Ainterface is usable bonding area and p is square-array pitch. Halving the pitch ideally quadruples the number of available connection sites in the same area. Some sites carry data while others provide clocks, control, power, and ground, so total joint count is not equal to interface data width. Finer pitch also reduces alignment and defect tolerances.
science.assumptions: Ideal square array without edge losses, keep-outs, unequal pitches, missing joints, or power-routing constraints. It is a geometric upper estimate and does not assert a Blackwell bump count or pitch.

name: Package substrate
role: Fans dense chip connections out to a mechanically supported interface with the circuit board.
description: The package substrate is a multilayer wiring and support structure beneath the dies and their dense interconnect platform. It carries signals, power, and ground through patterned copper, insulating layers, and vias. The connection spacing grows as routes move from the die side toward the board side. Power and signal integrity depend on routing geometry and return paths, not simply on how many wires fit. The substrate also helps manage mechanical loads and must cope with different thermal expansion among silicon, copper, and organic materials. In the atlas, peel its layers apart and distinguish signal traces from broad power planes. This shows why the green or brown platform under a processor is an engineered electrical structure rather than passive packaging.

mechanism: Dense die-side connections enter a stack of copper routes, dielectric layers, and vias.
Signal routes and power planes distribute connections across the package while preserving useful return paths and supply quality.
Larger-pitch terminals connect the package to the board, and the substrate supports mechanical and thermal loads.

Every route carries both signals and coolant.

science.title: The supply path must stay below a target impedance
science.explanation: ΔVallowed is the permissible rail-voltage excursion and ΔIstep is a change in load current. Their ratio sets an impedance target for the power delivery network. The substrate, board planes, vias, capacitors, and regulator jointly determine whether that target can be approached over the relevant frequencies. A connection that looks adequate at DC may still have too much transient impedance.
science.assumptions: A design target derived from a specified load step and voltage tolerance, not a complete stability proof. Frequency-dependent inductance, resonances, control response, and package parasitics must be analyzed; no vendor rail tolerance is supplied.

name: Thermal interface material
role: Fills microscopic gaps so heat can cross from a chip or lid into a cooling surface.
description: Two apparently flat solids touch only at small high points. Air trapped between them creates a poor thermal path. A thermal interface material conforms to those gaps and helps heat flow from the die or heat spreader toward the cooler. Performance depends on conductivity, thickness, contact pressure, surface finish, and long-term stability; a high conductivity number alone does not describe the complete joint. Some materials soften or change phase during operation, while others are greases, pads, or specialized bonded interfaces. The atlas should magnify the rough surfaces and show heat crossing the filled gap, then zoom out to the package heat path. A listed material example is a comparison anchor, not an assertion about NVIDIA’s proprietary thermal stack.

mechanism: The material fills microscopic gaps between the hot component and the mating cooling surface.
Contact pressure and operating conditions establish the effective bond line and its thermal resistance.
Heat conducts across the joint toward the next cooling layer while the material must remain stable over time.
misconception: Thermal conductivity alone does not specify interface performance. Thickness, contact pressure, surface condition, and aging also influence the installed thermal resistance.

check.question: Why can two materials with similar conductivity perform differently in a real assembly?
options: One of them stores more model parameters.
Their installed thickness, contact, and stability can differ.
Heat transfer is independent of geometry.
check.explanation: The thermal path is a physical joint, not just a material number. Contact and geometry can dominate the resulting temperature rise.

science.title: Geometry converts conductivity into resistance
science.explanation: t is interface thickness in meters, k is conductivity in W/(m·K), and A is contact area in square meters. Thermal resistance is measured in K/W; multiplying it by heat flow Q̇ in watts gives temperature rise. This separates a material property from an installed joint: the same material can perform differently when the bond line is thicker or the effective contact area is smaller.
science.assumptions: One-dimensional steady conduction through a uniform layer. Real joints add surface contact resistance, voids, nonuniform pressure, spreading, and aging; the bulk relation alone is not a package thermal rating.

name: Lid and heat spreader
role: Protects the package and spreads concentrated die heat toward a larger cooling contact.
description: A heat spreader is a thermally conductive cover used in many processor packages. It redistributes heat from a concentrated die region across a larger area and provides a robust mating surface for cooling hardware. Its presence adds another material and usually another interface to the heat path. Some high-performance designs instead use a lidless or direct-die arrangement, making contact closer to the silicon but demanding careful mechanical control. The atlas should provide both conceptual stackups rather than imply that every accelerator has the same lid. A heat spreader does not dispose of energy by itself: the heat still has to pass into a cooler and eventually leave the facility. Its shape and mounting are part of a complete thermal and mechanical design.

whyAI: AI chips concentrate large power in small areas. Managing that heat concentration supports stable operation across long training or inference runs.

mechanism: Heat leaves the active silicon through the die-side thermal interface.
The conductive cover spreads some of that concentrated heat laterally across a larger contact region.
The cooling assembly receives the heat through its own contact interface and carries it onward.
misconception: A heat spreader does not make heat disappear. It redistributes heat, which still has to leave through a cooler and the facility thermal system.

check.question: What is a key tradeoff between lidded and direct-die cooling?
options: A lid offers protection and spreading but adds material and interfaces to the heat path.
A lid makes cooling independent of power consumption.
Direct-die contact always requires no mechanical engineering.
check.explanation: Removing a lid can shorten the thermal path, but safe contact with fragile silicon requires careful mechanical and assembly control.

science.title: Every layer contributes to the thermal path
science.explanation: Rθ,i represents each serial thermal resistance between the active silicon and the coolant, including materials and contacts. The lid can spread heat over a larger area but also inserts material and interfaces. This relation helps viewers account for the complete path instead of attributing junction temperature only to the cooling fluid or the conductivity of one layer.
science.assumptions: A lumped steady-state series network with a common heat flow. Real packages have parallel paths, spatial hotspots, spreading resistance, and transient heat capacity; detailed temperatures require an appropriate thermal model.

name: Liquid-cooling coldplate
role: Captures heat at the processor and transfers it into flowing coolant.
description: A coldplate places a network of channels close to the heat source. Heat conducts through its metal base and enters coolant moving across the internal surfaces. Increasing contact area with small channels can improve heat transfer, but those channels also resist flow. The plate, pump, plumbing, coolant, and allowed temperatures therefore have to be designed together. The atlas should make the metal partly transparent so viewers can follow coolant from the inlet across hot regions to the outlet. Use a color change for coolant temperature rather than implying that blue liquid is electricity. The warmed coolant still carries energy that must be transferred through the rack and facility cooling chain; the plate is only the point where that journey begins.

scale: Centimeter-scale plate with submillimeter channel features; schematic geometry
mechanism: Heat conducts from the package through the plate’s base into the internal channel surfaces.
Coolant flowing over those surfaces absorbs thermal energy and warms as it crosses the plate.
The outlet carries warmed coolant to the larger cooling loop, where energy is transferred onward and the fluid is conditioned for reuse.
misconception: Blue and red coolant in the atlas encode temperature, not electrical charge. The liquid transports heat; the chip receives power through a separate electrical path.

check.question: Why can very small channels create a cooling tradeoff?
options: They remove the need for a pump.
They turn coolant into stored model weights.
They can improve heat transfer while increasing resistance to fluid flow.
check.explanation: More surface area can help heat exchange, but greater pressure drop raises pumping requirements and complicates flow distribution.

science.title: Flow and temperature rise account for captured heat
science.explanation: ṁ is coolant mass flow in kilograms per second and cp is specific heat capacity in J/(kg·K). Multiplying by the outlet-to-inlet temperature rise gives heat carried by the stream in watts. This measures transported energy, not the die temperature: the chip-to-fluid resistance still determines how hot the silicon must become to transfer that heat.
science.assumptions: Steady flow of a single-phase coolant with nearly constant heat capacity, negligible heat leakage, and no significant pressure-work or kinetic-energy change. Boiling and mixed-flow loops require a more general enthalpy balance.

name: Host CPU
role: Runs the operating system and coordinates the workloads, data preparation, and I/O surrounding accelerated computation.
description: The CPU is the general-purpose processor that organizes the system’s work. It runs operating-system services, prepares tasks, launches GPU kernels, handles control-heavy code, and coordinates data and networking. GPUs accelerate many numerical operations, but a full AI service still needs request handling, tokenization, orchestration, memory management, and failure recovery. In a Grace Blackwell system, the CPU and GPUs have a coherent high-bandwidth connection; in other servers, the host path commonly uses PCIe. Neither arrangement makes software coordination free. The atlas should show the CPU issuing a workload, allowing the GPU to run in parallel, and responding to completion. Separate control traffic from the much larger movement of tensor data so the division of labor becomes clear.

specs.label: Grace core count
specs.context: Per Grace CPU in the official GB200 configuration.

specs.label: GB200 pairing
specs.context: Per Grace Blackwell Superchip.

specs.label: CPU–GPU interconnect
specs.context: Interface rating; useful application bandwidth is workload dependent.

tradeoff: A faster accelerator can expose CPU scheduling or preprocessing bottlenecks. Moving more work onto the GPU helps some pipelines while making others harder to coordinate.
whyAI: An AI model becomes a usable service only when its numerical work is integrated with ordinary software tasks. The CPU supplies much of that general-purpose coordination.

sources.title: NVIDIA Data Center CPUs: Grace architecture
Intel Advisor: Amdahl’s Law and measurement
Intel: Announcing a New Era of Integrated Electronics

scale: Centimeter-scale packaged processor; functional blocks schematic
mechanism: The CPU runs the software that receives requests, prepares data, and organizes the computation.
It dispatches suitable numerical work to GPUs while continuing other control and system tasks.
Completion events and results return to the software pipeline for subsequent processing, response delivery, or recovery.
misconception: A fast GPU does not remove the need for general-purpose system software. CPU preparation, dispatch, and I/O coordination can still limit the overall service.

check.question: Which task naturally belongs to the CPU’s coordination role?
options: Serving as the liquid coolant.
Running the operating system and launching accelerator work.
Storing all HBM bits in one register.
check.explanation: The CPU integrates accelerated numerical work into a functioning software system, including control-heavy and operating-system responsibilities.

science.title: The unaccelerated fraction limits total speedup
science.explanation: f is the fraction of original execution time that a proposed accelerator can speed up, and s is its speedup for that portion. The remaining fraction includes tasks such as preparation, dispatch, serialization, or service logic. Even an arbitrarily fast GPU cannot eliminate time spent elsewhere. Measuring the complete application reveals which part deserves optimization next.
science.assumptions: Amdahl’s fixed-workload model with unchanged serial work and no added transfer or coordination overhead. Real batching, overlap, and workload scaling can alter the fractions; a peak hardware throughput ratio is not automatically s.

history.title: Intel introduces the 4004 microprocessor
history.significance: Intel introduced the 4004 in November 1971. Integrating a programmable CPU on a chip made it practical to reuse a hardware design for different instruction sequences, advancing the general-purpose control layer that still coordinates modern accelerator systems.

source.title: Intel: Announcing a New Era of Integrated Electronics

name: DDR5 server memory
role: Provides expandable main memory for conventional host CPUs and their software working sets.
description: DDR memory modules connect to a CPU’s memory channels and hold the working state of programs while powered. They provide substantially more capacity than small processor caches and are commonly socketed for service or expansion. DDR5 divides a module’s data interface into independent subchannels and introduces reliability features within the DRAM. On-die error correction is not the same as end-to-end protection of the complete memory link. This atlas includes DDR5 as the conventional server branch: the Grace CPU in the GB200 reference system uses LPDDR5X instead. Show the DIMM feeding the CPU rather than placing it beside a GPU as an HBM substitute. Bandwidth depends on channel count, transfer rate, ranks, and the supported population of the motherboard.

specs.label: DDR5 data organization
specs.context: Data bits only; server ECC modules carry additional check bits.

specs.label: Example transfer rate
specs.context: DDR5 example, not a universal current maximum.

specs.label: Example payload peak
specs.context: Calculated as 4,800 million transfers/s × 8 bytes; before workload effects.

tradeoff: Socketed memory offers capacity and service flexibility, but wide board routes consume energy and constrain speed. Adding modules can change the supported operating rate and access behavior.
whyAI: Datasets, preprocessing buffers, retrieval indexes, and service state often live in host memory. Adequate capacity prevents expensive movement to slower storage.
scale: About 10-centimeter module class; multiple packaged DRAM devices
mechanism: The CPU memory controller selects a channel and issues read or write commands to installed modules.
DRAM devices activate and access the relevant rows, transferring values across the module’s data subchannels.
Host software uses those values for its working set while refresh and error-management mechanisms preserve reliable operation.
misconception: DDR5 on-die ECC protects internal DRAM operations; it is not a substitute for all end-to-end server memory error protection. Grace also uses LPDDR5X rather than these socketed DDR DIMMs.

check.question: At 4,800 MT/s and 64 data bits, what is the theoretical payload rate before workload effects?
check.explanation: Each transfer carries 8 data bytes. Multiplying 4.8 billion transfers per second by 8 bytes gives 38.4 billion bytes per second.

science.title: Clock cycles and transfer rate are different units
science.explanation: CL is CAS latency measured in memory clock cycles. Double-data-rate signaling performs two transfers per clock, so a transfer rate of r million transfers per second corresponds to half that clock frequency. The formula converts a timing count into nanoseconds, showing why a larger CL number at a faster transfer rate can still represent similar absolute latency.
science.assumptions: CAS timing conversion for DDR with two transfers per clock. It covers the column-read timing interval, not total CPU load latency, row activation, precharge, queues, refresh, or burst completion. Use the selected device’s supported CL and rate together.

name: Grace LPDDR5X memory
role: Provides the Grace CPU’s local main memory with short, energy-conscious package and board connections.
description: LPDDR5X is dynamic memory designed with strong attention to power efficiency. Grace uses it for CPU main memory, giving the host processor a local store distinct from the GPU’s HBM. Coherent CPU–GPU connectivity can simplify access to a shared address space, but it does not erase the physical difference between these memories or their paths. The atlas should show CPU memory and HBM as separate reservoirs linked through an interconnect, with costs visible when data moves between them. Capacity options and rated bandwidth vary by module configuration. Avoid combining an early architecture estimate with a later product capacity as if they were one guaranteed operating point. The useful question is which memory contains each part of the workload and how often that part must travel.

specs.label: GB200 CPU memory
specs.context: Per Grace Blackwell Superchip product table; configurations vary.

specs.label: Published bandwidth
specs.context: Product maximum; do not assume every capacity option achieves it.

specs.label: Storage role
specs.context: Distinct from GPU HBM3E despite coherent access support.

interfaces.name: Coherent GPU access

tradeoff: Closer memory integration can improve energy efficiency but offers different expansion and service options than socketed DIMMs. Coherent access is convenient, yet locality still affects performance.
whyAI: Host memory supports preparation, orchestration, and data that do not reside permanently in HBM. Efficient placement avoids turning the CPU–GPU link into an unnecessary bottleneck.
scale: Memory packages near the Grace CPU; exact module layout varies
mechanism: Grace keeps CPU-resident program and data state in its local LPDDR5X memory subsystem.
The CPU reads and updates that state through its memory controllers.
When GPU work needs data located there, the coherent interconnect provides a path while preserving the distinction between physical memory locations.
misconception: A coherent address space does not merge CPU LPDDR and GPU HBM into one memory with identical performance. The physical route to each location still matters.

check.question: Why distinguish CPU LPDDR from GPU HBM in a coherent system?
options: Coherence means no bits ever move between components.
They are the same physical memory chips under two names.
They have different capacities, bandwidths, and access paths.
check.explanation: Coherence simplifies some programming tasks, but good placement still avoids unnecessary transfers between physically different memory systems.

science.title: Coherence does not remove path bottlenecks
science.explanation: Each B is effective payload bandwidth at the relevant one-direction path boundary. Reading CPU-resident data from a GPU must traverse both the CPU memory subsystem and the interconnect, even when a coherent address space makes that access convenient. Capacity can be shared logically without turning every memory location into an equally fast physical resource.
science.assumptions: A serial-path upper bound for sustained transfers with adequate concurrency. Cache hits, compression, competing traffic, routing, and write/read direction change the applicable boundaries; do not substitute a summed bidirectional rating for one-way payload bandwidth.

history.title: Grace CPU Superchip announces server LPDDR5X integration
history.significance: The March 2022 Grace CPU Superchip announcement described an LPDDR5X memory subsystem with error correction in a data-center CPU platform. This is a Grace platform milestone, not the invention of LPDDR memory.

name: PCI Express interconnect
role: Connects host processors, accelerators, storage, and network adapters through standardized serial links.
description: PCIe is a general-purpose component interconnect built from serial lanes. A link can use several lanes in parallel, and switches can connect multiple devices into a hierarchy. Transactions carry commands and data; software uses drivers and device capabilities to arrange transfers. The generation and lane count must both be stated when comparing bandwidth. A faster endpoint may operate at a lower rate when the host, switch, or board path supports less. The atlas should show separate transmit and receive lanes and reveal packet overhead, so an advertised bidirectional number is not mistaken for one-way application throughput. PCIe is one part of the AI system’s connectivity, alongside specialized coherent links, GPU scale-up fabrics, and the network between servers.

specs.label: PCIe 5.0 signaling
specs.context: Raw transfer rate; payload bandwidth is lower.

specs.label: PCIe 6.0 signaling
specs.context: Uses PAM4, FLIT encoding, and forward error correction.

specs.label: PCIe 6.0 ×16
specs.context: 128 GB/s each direction before protocol overhead; not a GB200 board-wide guarantee.

interfaces.name: Link training
interfaces.signal: Negotiated width, speed, and signal equalization

tradeoff: Higher speeds increase transfer capacity but tighten electrical and board-design requirements. Real throughput also depends on packet overhead, topology, transfer size, and device behavior.
whyAI: NICs and NVMe drives use PCIe to deliver data into the compute system. Congestion on these paths can starve accelerators even when the GPUs themselves are fast.

sources.title: Intel: PCI Express Gen4/Gen5 architecture and encoding

scale: Centimeter board traces and connectors; logical lane pairs enlarged
mechanism: The endpoints train a link and agree on a supported speed and lane width.
Transactions are packetized and serialized across separate transmit and receive paths.
The receiving device handles requests or data and sends completions as required by the protocol.
misconception: GT/s, GB/s, and bidirectional aggregate bandwidth are different measures. A raw line rate must account for lane count, direction, and protocol overhead before comparison with application throughput.

check.question: What happens if a fast PCIe device is connected through a slower supported host path?
options: The link must always use the device’s maximum advertised generation.
It operates at a mutually supported speed and width.
It automatically becomes an NVLink interface.
check.explanation: PCIe capability is negotiated across the actual link. The endpoint, host, switches, and board support determine what is usable.

science.title: Encoding and protocol reduce raw lane bandwidth
science.explanation: For a Gen5 link, each lane runs at 32 GT/s with 128b/130b encoding. Sixteen lanes yield about 63.0 GB/s per direction after this encoding overhead, before transaction and link-protocol costs. Full-duplex operation can carry traffic both ways, but summing the directions does not make a single transfer twice as fast.
science.assumptions: PCIe Gen5 at negotiated full lane width, using NRZ and 128b/130b encoding. Excludes packet headers, flow control, acknowledgments, and implementation limits. PCIe Gen6 uses a different signaling and FLIT model and must be calculated separately.

name: Network interface adapter
role: Moves data between the server and the cluster network, often with direct-memory and protocol offloads.
description: A NIC converts server memory transfers into network packets and receives packets from other machines. High-performance adapters can perform remote direct memory access, allowing registered buffers to be transferred with less involvement from the remote CPU. GPU-aware paths can also reduce unnecessary staging through host memory when the platform and software support them. These capabilities do not eliminate synchronization, congestion, or network topology. The atlas should show a tensor fragment leaving a GPU buffer, passing through the adapter, and joining a remote buffer, while a separate small control path manages the operation. The NIC belongs to the scale-out path between systems; it should not be confused with NVLink’s local GPU fabric or with the ordinary management network.

specs.label: ConnectX-7 example
specs.context: NVIDIA adapter family rating; selected card and port modes vary.

specs.label: Byte-rate equivalent
specs.context: Arithmetic conversion before protocol overhead; not 400 GB/s.

specs.label: Acceleration
specs.context: Availability depends on adapter, firmware, topology, and software.

interfaces.name: Local memory transfer
interfaces.signal: Registered host or supported GPU buffers

tradeoff: Faster ports help only if the host path and network can sustain them. Queueing, congestion control, and placement can dominate tail latency even below the nominal line rate.
whyAI: Distributed training exchanges gradients and parameters across servers. Distributed inference and storage access also depend on efficient movement beyond one rack’s local GPU domain.
scale: Centimeter-scale adapter or module with external copper/optical links
mechanism: Software or a supported accelerator path identifies buffers and initiates a network operation.
The NIC reads data, applies the appropriate protocol processing, and transmits packets through the network.
The remote adapter places received data into supported buffers and reports completion so dependent work can continue.
misconception: A 400 Gb/s port is not a 400 GB/s port. Dividing by eight gives 50 GB/s before network and protocol overhead.

check.question: What does RDMA principally reduce in a supported transfer?
options: The remote CPU’s work copying and processing the payload.
The number of bits in the model vocabulary.
The need for any network fabric.
check.explanation: RDMA places data directly into registered memory with less remote CPU intervention. It still requires a functioning network, protocol, and synchronization.

science.title: Small messages and large transfers have different bottlenecks
science.explanation: α represents fixed software, adapter, and path latency; M is payload bytes; Bpayload is sustained payload bandwidth in bytes per second. For small M, startup dominates. For large M, bandwidth dominates. This explains why buying a faster line-rate adapter may help bulk gradient transfers more than tiny synchronization messages, and why scheduling and aggregation matter.
science.assumptions: A single uncontended path and approximately constant startup cost. Congestion, multiple hops, retransmission, protocol offloads, and overlap can change both terms. Convert bits per second to bytes per second before comparing them.

name: NVMe solid-state storage
role: Persists datasets, model checkpoints, and software beyond power cycles.
description: An NVMe SSD combines nonvolatile NAND flash, a controller, firmware, and a fast host interface. It stores data persistently rather than providing the byte-addressable working memory used directly by arithmetic units. The controller maps logical blocks to flash locations, handles error management, and schedules reads and writes across internal parallelism. Large sequential transfers and small random accesses stress different parts of the device, so one speed number cannot describe every workload. The atlas should follow a model checkpoint from persistent storage into host or GPU memory, then distinguish that loading phase from repeated tensor computation. Supported direct-storage paths can reduce extra copies, but the storage device still has its own latency, bandwidth, and endurance limits.

specs.context: Vendor-rated maximum; capacity, host, and test conditions matter.

specs.label: Sequential write
specs.context: Micron 9550 selected configurations; not all capacities reach this.

specs.label: Host protocol
specs.context: The protocol and physical interface are distinct layers.

interfaces.name: Persistent data
interfaces.signal: Dataset batches, model files, and checkpoints

tradeoff: Storage offers durable capacity but is far slower than on-chip memory and HBM. Checkpoint frequency trades recovery effort against write traffic and interruption to useful work.
whyAI: Training begins with stored data and produces checkpoints that must survive failures. Serving systems also need to load and update model artifacts reliably.

sources.title: John D. C. Little (2011): Little’s Law and computer architecture applications

scale: Centimeter-scale module containing controller and NAND packages
mechanism: The host issues block requests through the NVMe protocol to the SSD controller.
The controller maps those requests onto flash operations and uses internal parallelism and error handling to read or write data.
Data are loaded into working memory for computation, while completed checkpoints can be committed back to persistent storage.
misconception: NVMe storage capacity is not interchangeable with HBM capacity. Storage persists without power but has a different access model and much higher access cost.

check.question: Why is a saved checkpoint useful after a node loses power?
options: It remains in a powered-off GPU register.
It changes the physical number of Tensor Cores.
A nonvolatile storage copy survives when volatile working memory is lost.
check.explanation: Checkpoints persist the state needed for recovery. Their usefulness depends on what was saved and how recently it was committed.

science.title: High IOPS requires enough outstanding work
science.explanation: Queue depth is the average number of operations in flight, IOPS is completed operations per second, and L is average latency in seconds. A drive capable of high throughput can remain underused if the application submits one request and waits before issuing the next. Increasing concurrency helps only until the storage, host link, or workload becomes the bottleneck.
science.assumptions: Little’s law applied to a stable workload with a consistent measurement boundary. Latency generally changes with load, so the relation does not promise constant latency at arbitrary queue depth; read size, write mix, and durability requirements matter.

name: Voltage regulator module
role: Converts a distribution voltage into tightly controlled low-voltage rails for processors and memory.
description: A VRM sits electrically between the power distribution system and the chip. Switching stages, inductors, capacitors, and a controller turn an incoming supply into the rail the load needs. Multiple phases share current and can reduce ripple while responding to rapid changes in demand. GPU activity changes quickly as kernels start, synchronize, or wait for data, so stable voltage requires more than matching average power. The atlas should animate current through alternating phases and show capacitors supporting a sudden load step. Use illustrative voltages where product values are not public. A large current is compatible with a modest voltage because power is their product; this explains why short, low-resistance connections matter so much near the silicon.

specs.label: Conversion principle
specs.context: A 1,000 W load at an illustrative 1 V requires 1,000 A, excluding conversion loss.

specs.label: Reference conversion
specs.context: TI reference design example; not a GB200 power-stage specification.

specs.label: Control architecture
specs.context: Current sharing and transient response are design objectives.

tradeoff: More phases and larger filters can improve current delivery but occupy board space and add losses or cost. The best operating point balances efficiency, stability, response, and temperature.
whyAI: Every arithmetic operation depends on a stable electrical supply. Poor transient response or excessive distribution loss can limit the usable compute power of the accelerator.

Texas Instruments: 48 V to 12 V, 1.1 kW converter reference design
Texas Instruments: Basic calculation of a buck converter power stage

scale: Centimeter-scale circuit around the processor; millimeter power components
mechanism: Switching stages draw energy from the incoming DC distribution rail in controlled intervals.
Inductors and capacitors smooth the output while multiple phases share the demanded current.
Feedback adjusts switching as the processor load changes, keeping the supply rail within its required operating limits.
misconception: Low chip voltage does not imply low electrical current. At a fixed power, lower voltage requires more current, making distribution resistance and transients important.

check.question: At an illustrative 1 V, how much current corresponds to a 1,000 W load?
check.explanation: Using P = V × I gives I = 1,000 W / 1 V = 1,000 A. This is an illustration, not an asserted GPU rail specification.

science.title: Inductor volt-seconds set the ideal buck ratio
science.explanation: D is switch-on fraction of each cycle, L is phase inductance, and fs is switching frequency. A buck converter alternates charging and discharging the inductor; average inductor voltage must be zero in steady operation. The ripple relation shows how inductance and switching frequency affect phase-current variation, which interacts with capacitor choice and transient response.
science.assumptions: Ideal continuous-conduction buck stage with fixed input/output voltage and negligible switch losses. Multiphase cancellation, nonlinear inductors, dead time, control dynamics, and discontinuous conduction require further analysis; no GPU power-stage values are assumed.

name: Power supply and power shelf
role: Converts facility power into the regulated DC distribution used by the compute rack.
description: A power supply converts incoming electrical power into a form the equipment can distribute and use. Rack systems combine several supplies in shelves, sharing load and providing redundancy. A shelf’s installed nameplate capacity is not the same as the power continuously consumed by the rack, especially when redundant capacity is reserved. Efficiency also varies with load, and conversion loss becomes heat that must be removed. The atlas should show facility input splitting across supplies, joining the DC distribution path, and continuing toward board regulators. A failure scenario can remove one supply path while the remaining capacity carries the load, making reliability tangible. Exact supply counts and redundancy arrangements should remain tied to the named rack design.

whyAI: Large AI systems are constrained by deliverable electrical power as well as chip count. Power shelves turn facility capacity into a controlled supply that accelerators can actually consume.

scale: Rack shelf scale with multiple centimeter-scale supply modules
mechanism: Incoming facility power is converted into the DC supply used by the rack distribution system.
Multiple power modules share the load, with extra capacity arranged according to the required redundancy strategy.
DC power feeds downstream regulators, while telemetry and protection respond to changing demand or faults.
misconception: Installed PSU capacity is not the rack’s constant power consumption. Redundancy reserves capacity, and actual load depends on equipment and operating workload.

check.question: Why can a rack have more installed PSU capacity than its normal consumption?
options: Some capacity is reserved for redundancy and operating margin.
The unused rating proves the rack consumes no electricity.
Power supplies permanently store spare compute instructions.
check.explanation: Redundant designs preserve enough capacity when a supply path fails or is serviced. The installed rating and active consumption therefore describe different things.

science.title: Conversion loss becomes a cooling load
science.explanation: Efficiency η relates useful DC output power to electrical input. The difference is dissipated in the conversion system. At large rack loads, even a small efficiency change can alter the heat that power shelves and facility cooling must remove. Installed redundant capacity is a separate concept: it changes the available power paths, not this conservation-of-energy accounting.
science.assumptions: Steady average power at explicitly chosen input and output boundaries. Efficiency depends on voltage, load, and operating conditions; other rack and facility losses are outside a supply-only calculation.

name: Compute baseboard and tray
role: Integrates processors, memory, adapters, power, cooling, and service interfaces into an operational node.
description: The baseboard is where separate components become a coordinated machine. Its traces and connectors join processors, memory, storage, network adapters, management, and power circuits. A compute tray adds mechanical support, cooling connections, and interfaces that let the assembly slide into a rack. Topology matters: which GPU reaches which NIC, which devices share a PCIe path, and where CPU memory sits can all affect performance. The atlas should peel the board into signal, power, and cooling views, then allow one tensor or watt to be followed through the assembly. This view is a logical reconstruction based on published block diagrams, not a manufacturing drawing. The serviceable tray is the bridge between package-scale engineering and rack-scale operations.

whyAI: The GPU’s performance is useful only when data, power, and heat can move through the surrounding node. The tray makes those dependencies physically explicit.

mechanism: The board physically mounts the computing, memory, I/O, control, and power components and connects their electrical interfaces.
The tray integrates that board with structural support, cooling paths, and rack-facing connectors.
Power, data, management, and heat flow through separate but coordinated paths while the node executes its workload.
misconception: A compute tray is not just a row of GPUs. CPU affinity, network paths, power delivery, cooling, and service connections all affect its practical behavior.

check.question: Why inspect a compute tray’s topology before distributing a workload?
options: Every component has an identical path to every other component.
Topology only changes the tray’s appearance.
Shared links and device proximity can change communication costs.
check.explanation: Topology reveals which paths are local, shared, or remote. Work placement can avoid unnecessary traffic and contention.

science.title: Impedance discontinuities reflect fast signals
science.explanation: Z0 is the transmission-line characteristic impedance and Zload is the termination impedance. Γ is the voltage reflection coefficient: a matched resistive load gives zero reflection, an open approaches +1, and a short approaches −1. Traces, vias, connectors, and package transitions must be designed together because reflected energy can distort the eye opening used to distinguish high-speed bits.
science.assumptions: An ideal linear transmission line at a single termination, with real resistances for the simple limiting examples. Loss, frequency-dependent impedance, differential coupling, equalization, and multiple discontinuities require fuller channel analysis.

name: Baseboard management controller
role: Monitors and controls hardware through a management path separate from the main workload.
description: The BMC is a small management computer that remains useful when the main operating system is unavailable. It collects sensor readings, exposes hardware status, and supports operations such as power control and remote maintenance through a separate network. In large AI installations, this out-of-band view helps operators locate failing components and coordinate recovery. It should not be confused with the CPU running the model service or a NIC carrying training tensors. The atlas should draw management connections with a distinct color and show them reaching compute trays, power equipment, and switches. A healthy management path does not mean the workload is healthy, but it provides the observations and controls needed to diagnose the physical system.

specs.label: Network role
specs.context: Distinct from the data and GPU communication networks.

specs.label: Observed state
specs.context: Exact sensors and controls depend on the device.

specs.label: DGX management endpoints
specs.value: Compute trays, switches, and power shelves
specs.context: Documented rack management network scope.

interfaces.name: Sensors
interfaces.signal: Temperatures, power readings, and hardware status

tradeoff: A separate controller improves observability and recovery, but adds firmware and network components to maintain. Management access and workload traffic should have clearly defined roles.
whyAI: Thousands of accelerators require coordinated monitoring and repair. Management controllers help turn a collection of chips into infrastructure that can stay available over long jobs.

sources.title: NVIDIA DGX GB rack systems networking guide

scale: Small board controller and rack-wide logical management paths
mechanism: The controller collects hardware sensor readings and device status through management interfaces.
It exposes that information over an out-of-band network independent of the main application data path.
Authorized operators or automation use the observations and controls to diagnose faults, change power state, or coordinate recovery.
misconception: A healthy BMC connection does not prove the GPU workload or operating system is healthy. It provides a separate way to observe and control the hardware.

check.question: Why keep management traffic separate from training tensors?
options: Management should replace all high-bandwidth GPU communication.
A distinct path helps operators observe and recover hardware when the main workload path fails.
The BMC must calculate all model attention scores.
check.explanation: Out-of-band management improves access to hardware state during failures or maintenance without making it part of the main numerical data path.

science.title: Polling cadence limits fault detection delay
science.explanation: Δt is the interval between equally spaced sensor checks. If a persistent fault starts at a uniformly random phase between checks, its average wait to the next observation is half the interval. Faster polling improves detection opportunity but produces more telemetry and processing. Event-driven alerts can supplement polling, while recovery time after detection remains a separate part of availability.
science.assumptions: An ideal persistent, immediately observable fault with uniformly distributed start time, perfect polling, and zero collection/transport delay. Brief faults, missed checks, thresholds, retries, and alert pipelines change the result. This is a monitoring model, not a vendor BMC guarantee.

name: Grace Blackwell Superchip
role: Couples one Grace CPU with two Blackwell GPUs so host and accelerator work can share a tightly integrated system.
description: The Grace Blackwell Superchip is a system integration unit, not one monolithic piece of silicon. It combines one CPU and two GPUs, with separate CPU memory and GPU HBM connected through a coherent interconnect. The GPUs also participate in a larger NVLink domain when installed in an NVL72 rack. This published reference explains a modern architecture; it is not evidence about the hardware used by any specific proprietary model service.

role: Matches queued workloads to available compute resources under operational policies.
description: A cluster scheduler turns shared hardware into an organized service.
