The atlas shows requests entering a queue, resource groups being reserved, and workers launching on those allocations. It distinguishes this job-level decision from the GPU hardware scheduler that issues instructions and from the serving scheduler that batches inference requests. Good placement can improve communication locality, but a scheduler cannot remove the algorithm's communication requirements or manufacture capacity that the cluster does not have.

specs.label: Example system
specs.context: GPU-aware resource allocation.

specs.label: Allocation inputs
specs.context: Actual rules depend on the installation.

specs.label: Boundary
specs.context: Distinct from kernel instruction scheduling.

tradeoff: Packing improves utilization. Queue fairness, locality, and job constraints can compete.
whyAI: Large training jobs need coordinated resource reservations. Allocation decisions influence waiting time and communication placement.

sources.title: MIT — Queueing Models and Little’s Law

scale: Cluster-wide logical control plane
mechanism: Read a job’s resource request and policy constraints.
Choose an available compatible allocation.
Launch and track the job while releasing resources when it finishes.
misconception: Cluster scheduling and GPU instruction scheduling occur at different levels of the machinery.

check.question: What does a cluster scheduler primarily decide?
options: Which available resources a job receives
The position of every electron in a GPU
The next token probability inside a model
check.explanation: It allocates and manages execution resources; lower software and hardware layers execute the assigned workload.

science.title: Little’s law
science.explanation: Average in-system job count L equals admitted arrival rate λ times average time W spent within the chosen system boundary. It links workload concurrency to waiting and service time.
science.assumptions: Stable long-run averages with consistent arrival and population definitions; not a prediction of each job’s latency or an overloaded transient queue.

name: CUDA programming and runtime layer
role: Provides a software model and interfaces for executing parallel work on NVIDIA GPUs.
description: CUDA connects host-side programs to GPU execution. A program prepares data, invokes device work, and coordinates memory and synchronization through runtime or driver interfaces and libraries. The programming model gives developers a way to describe many related operations without manually addressing every physical arithmetic lane. Frameworks commonly use CUDA indirectly through optimized libraries or generated kernels. The atlas represents this layer as a translation boundary between tensor operations and device launches, not as a physical chip component. CUDA alone is not an AI model, a complete training framework, or a promise of optimal performance. Data movement, launch structure, numerical formats, and kernel behavior still determine how well the application uses the hardware.

specs.label: Execution roles
specs.context: Cooperating CPU-side control and GPU-side work.

specs.label: Work expression
specs.context: Frameworks may call these indirectly.

specs.label: Scope
specs.context: Other accelerator ecosystems have different interfaces.

tradeoff: High-level interfaces improve programmability. Efficient execution still requires suitable algorithms and memory behavior.
whyAI: CUDA is one major bridge from AI frameworks to accelerators. It helps software turn tensor operations into executable device work.

sources.title: Hill and Marty — Amdahl’s Law in the Multicore Era

scale: Software abstraction; no physical size
mechanism: Prepare operations and data from the host-side application.
Invoke GPU kernels or accelerated library routines.
Coordinate completion and use the produced results in later work.
misconception: CUDA is a programming platform, not a neural network and not a transistor-level execution diagram.

check.question: Where can an AI framework use CUDA?
options: Only during wafer fabrication
Through runtime interfaces, libraries, or generated GPU kernels
Only after a model reaches AGI
check.explanation: Framework operations can dispatch work through several CUDA-layer mechanisms, often without users writing kernels directly.

science.title: Amdahl speedup bound
science.explanation: If fraction p of baseline time can be accelerated N-fold, the remaining fraction still limits total speedup. Host work and transfers can therefore dominate after a GPU kernel becomes very fast.
science.assumptions: Fixed workload, ideal acceleration of the selected fraction, and no added overhead; real GPU applications may have additional communication and scaling effects.

name: GPU kernel and thread hierarchy
role: Maps an operation onto many coordinated logical threads or tiles.
description: A GPU kernel is a unit of device code launched with an execution configuration. In CUDA's thread model, threads are grouped into blocks, and blocks form a grid. A block executes on a streaming multiprocessor and can use block-level shared memory and synchronization. The grid may contain far more blocks than the device can host simultaneously, so the logical grid is not a physical map of dedicated cores. The atlas animates blocks being assigned to available processors while preserving the distinction between work items and hardware. Efficient kernels arrange data access and reuse carefully. Arbitrary cross-block waiting is unsafe in a normal launch because blocks are not guaranteed to run in a particular order.

specs.label: Thread-model hierarchy
specs.context: Logical launch organization.

specs.label: Warp size
specs.context: Execution grouping in the documented programming model.

specs.label: Normal block ordering
specs.context: Special supported cooperative mechanisms have additional rules.

interfaces.name: Input tensors and launch shape
interfaces.signal: Data pointers and parallel work configuration

tradeoff: More parallel work can hide latency. Register use, shared memory, divergence, and data access constrain useful occupancy.
whyAI: Kernels implement the actual tensor operations on GPUs. Tiling and reuse can matter as much as raw arithmetic capability.
scale: Logical work grid mapped over physical GPU resources
mechanism: Divide the operation into indexed work items or tiles.
Launch blocks that the device assigns to available execution resources.
Reuse and synchronize data within supported boundaries, then write the result.
misconception: One launched thread is not one permanently dedicated physical GPU core; logical work is scheduled onto shared hardware.

check.question: Can a normal kernel assume all grid blocks run simultaneously?
options: Yes, every block has its own permanent core
Yes, if the grid is colored uniformly
No; block scheduling and order are not generally guaranteed
check.explanation: A grid can exceed the device’s resident capacity, so ordinary cross-block dependencies must respect the programming model.

science.title: Roofline model
science.equation: I = FLOPs / bytes moved; R ≤ min(P_peak, B_memory I)
science.explanation: Arithmetic intensity connects the operation count to traffic at a selected memory boundary. Tiling can raise intensity by reusing fetched data, shifting a kernel toward its arithmetic ceiling.
science.assumptions: Upper-bound model for a specified numeric format and memory level; measured performance is also limited by launch, occupancy, dependencies, and implementation details.

name: Compiler, intermediate code, and device executable
role: Transforms program descriptions into executable instructions and runtime-compatible artifacts.
description: Compilation bridges the form humans or frameworks express and the instructions hardware executes. In the CUDA toolchain, the compiler driver separates host and device portions, invokes the appropriate compilation stages, and packages device code for use by the host application. Intermediate representations support transformations before final device-specific code is produced, and some paths use runtime compilation. The atlas shows a graph passing through lowering and code-generation stages, with the final launch connected to GPU execution. Optimizations can combine or reorganize operations, but they must preserve the permitted program semantics. A faster compiler path does not change the trained model's intent; it changes how the same required work is mapped to available machinery.

specs.label: CUDA tool example
specs.context: Coordinates host and device compilation stages.

specs.label: Representations
specs.context: Exact stages depend on the toolchain and options.

specs.label: Correctness boundary
specs.context: Optimizations must respect specified numerical and execution behavior.

tradeoff: Specialization can improve execution efficiency. Compilation overhead and target dependence complicate deployment.
whyAI: Compilers map high-level tensor work onto device instructions. Their choices influence memory traffic, launch overhead, and hardware use.
scale: Software transformation graph; no physical size
mechanism: Analyze the program and its target requirements.
Lower and optimize host and device work through the toolchain.
Package or generate executable device code for runtime launch.
misconception: A compiler does not discover model weights by itself; training and program translation are different processes.

check.question: What is the compiler’s central job in this layer?
options: Transform program descriptions into executable forms
Provide emergency electrical power
Replace the training dataset with silicon
check.explanation: Compilation changes the representation and implementation of a program while preserving its required behavior.

science.title: Sequential execution-time decomposition
science.equation: T ≈ Σ t_launch + Σ t_kernel + Σ t_transfer
science.explanation: Compilation and fusion can change the number of launches, intermediate materializations, and execution kernels. This decomposition helps explain a speedup without assuming that fewer kernels always win.
science.assumptions: Illustrative sequential baseline without overlap; fused kernels may change register pressure, occupancy, numerical behavior, and actual execution costs.

name: Collective communication library
role: Coordinates group communication operations across participating GPUs.
description: Distributed computation often needs a group operation rather than an isolated message. An all-reduce combines contributions from every participating rank and makes the result available to each; all-gather and reduce-scatter have different input and output layouts. NCCL provides GPU-oriented implementations of these collective operations over supported communication paths. The atlas depicts ranks as participants and tensor segments as the objects being moved and combined, then overlays the underlying rack or network fabric. A ring is one useful teaching algorithm, not the only implementation. Communication correctness requires compatible participation and operation ordering. Its performance depends on message size, topology, available bandwidth, and how well communication overlaps with independent computation.

specs.label: All-reduce result
specs.context: Reduction operation such as sum is specified.

specs.label: Related collectives
specs.context: Different distribution semantics.

specs.label: Participants
specs.context: Logical membership, not necessarily one entire rack.

tradeoff: Collectives simplify distributed coordination. Synchronization and communication can become the dominant waiting cost.
whyAI: Training workers exchange gradients and sharded state. Collective operations connect those pieces into a consistent computation.
scale: Logical multi-GPU communication overlay
mechanism: Define the participating ranks and the collective operation.
Move and, when required, reduce tensor segments over supported paths.
Return the specified result layout to each participant.
misconception: All-reduce is a communication-and-reduction operation; it does not mean every worker retrains the entire model from scratch.

check.question: What does a sum all-reduce return?
options: Only the first rank’s original tensor
The sum of contributions to every participating rank
A new physical GPU
check.explanation: Each participant receives the reduced result, unlike a reduction that delivers only to one root.

science.title: All-reduce traffic normalization
science.explanation: For the conventional bandwidth accounting, all-reduce includes reduction and distribution traffic. NCCL tests normalize algorithm bandwidth using this factor so it can be compared with a communication bottleneck.
science.assumptions: P is rank count and S is bytes per rank; conventional point-to-point all-reduce model, not a universal traffic law for hardware-assisted reductions or every algorithm.

name: Data, tensor, pipeline, and state parallelism
role: Splits model work and state across devices to fit memory and exploit concurrent execution.
description: Parallel training has several independent axes. Data parallelism processes different examples with model replicas; tensor parallelism splits work inside layers; pipeline parallelism assigns different layer groups to stages. Other schemes partition sequence context, experts, or model state. These choices can be combined, but every partition creates communication and scheduling consequences. The atlas lets a viewer apply different splits to the same model diagram and observe which tensors must cross device boundaries. More GPUs are therefore not a universal speed multiplier. The best arrangement depends on model shape, sequence length, memory capacity, network topology, batch behavior, and the overhead of coordinating the pieces into one correct training or inference computation.

specs.label: Data parallelism
specs.context: Workers coordinate the resulting updates.

specs.label: Tensor / pipeline
specs.context: Different communication and scheduling patterns.

specs.label: State sharding
specs.context: Can reduce per-device memory use.

tradeoff: Partitioning increases usable capacity. Communication and pipeline idle time can reduce scaling efficiency.
whyAI: Large models often exceed one device’s practical resources. Parallelism makes their execution possible across a coordinated system.

sources.title: Narayanan et al. — Efficient Large-Scale Language Model Training

scale: Logical model-to-device mapping
mechanism: Choose which workload dimensions or state components to partition.
Assign the resulting pieces to devices with suitable connectivity.
Schedule computation and required exchanges so the complete operation remains correct.
misconception: Doubling GPU count does not guarantee halving runtime; communication and serial dependencies remain.

check.question: Which strategy splits work inside an individual layer?
options: Pipeline parallelism only
Data replication only
Tensor parallelism
check.explanation: Tensor parallelism divides a layer’s tensor computations; pipeline parallelism instead partitions groups of layers.

science.title: Global batch accounting
science.explanation: Data-parallel replicas contribute different examples. Tensor- and pipeline-parallel workers cooperate on those examples and therefore do not automatically multiply the effective global batch.
science.assumptions: Uniform per-replica microbatch and accumulation count; variable batches and specialized schedules require explicit accounting.

history.title: Large-model tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism analyzed together
history.significance: The Megatron-LM study quantified interactions between parallelism strategies, emphasizing that model partitioning and hardware communication must be designed together.

source.title: Narayanan et al. — Efficient Large-Scale Language Model Training

name: Distributed checkpoint and recovery state
role: Persists enough execution state to resume a model workflow after interruption.
description: A checkpoint records a recoverable state of a training or inference workflow. Training recovery often needs more than model weights: optimizer state, step information, and other application state may be required to resume correctly. Distributed checkpoint systems can save shards from multiple workers and restore them through a coordinated load path. The atlas shows memory-state pieces leaving workers for durable storage, then returning to a new allocation. This separates a checkpoint from the transient attention KV cache and from a copy of the original dataset. Save frequency trades write overhead against potential lost work. A checkpoint is useful only when its contents, metadata, and compatibility are sufficient for the intended recovery procedure.

specs.label: Training state
specs.context: Exact recovery requirements depend on the workload.

specs.label: Distributed storage
specs.context: Multiple workers can save and restore coordinated pieces.

specs.label: Purpose
specs.value: Resume or reuse a saved state
specs.context: Not the same as a live KV cache.

tradeoff: Frequent saves reduce potential lost progress. They add I/O and coordination overhead.
whyAI: Long training runs must tolerate interruptions. Checkpointing protects accumulated work and enables controlled continuation.
scale: Distributed software state persisted to storage
mechanism: Identify the state required for the intended recovery.
Write its shards and metadata to durable storage.
Load and coordinate those pieces when the workflow resumes.
misconception: Saving model weights alone may not preserve the optimizer and other state needed for faithful training continuation.

check.question: Which statement about a training checkpoint is correct?
options: It may need optimizer and application state in addition to weights
It is identical to the prompt’s KV cache
It guarantees infinite backup power
check.explanation: The required snapshot depends on what must be restored. Training state often extends beyond the parameter tensors.

science.title: Checkpoint write-time floor
science.explanation: Checkpoint size includes the actual state being persisted, and the relevant rate is sustainable end-to-end storage throughput. Metadata and coordination add costs beyond this lower bound.
science.assumptions: Ideal streaming lower bound over the chosen storage path; asynchronous saves may overlap work but do not eliminate traffic or consistency requirements.

name: Inference serving and request scheduling
role: Turns incoming model requests into scheduled prefill and generation work.
description: A serving engine manages the many requests that share an inference deployment. It receives inputs, schedules prompt processing, keeps track of generation state, and returns outputs while managing memory and latency goals. Continuous batching can admit and retire requests as generation progresses instead of waiting for one fixed batch to finish. Paged KV-cache management organizes attention state in blocks to reduce wasted allocation and support flexible scheduling. The atlas shows requests with different lengths sharing device execution while retaining distinct state. Serving optimization changes resource use and response timing, not the meaning of trained weights. Throughput, time to first token, and time between later tokens must be considered separately because users experience all three differently.

specs.label: Execution phases
specs.context: Prompt processing followed by iterative generation.

specs.label: Latency measures
specs.value: Time to first token and inter-token latency
specs.context: Different parts of perceived responsiveness.

specs.label: Example techniques
specs.value: Continuous batching and paged KV cache
specs.context: Documented in vLLM; implementation-specific.

tradeoff: Batching can improve throughput. Queueing and memory pressure can worsen individual request latency.
whyAI: Serving makes trained models available to people and applications. It translates hardware capacity into practical responsiveness and concurrency.

sources.title: Kwon et al. — Efficient Memory Management with PagedAttention

scale: Request-to-device software pipeline
mechanism: Accept requests and schedule their prompt processing.
Maintain each request’s state while batching compatible generation work.
Stream results and release resources as requests finish.
misconception: Higher tokens-per-second throughput does not automatically mean lower latency for one user’s request.

check.question: What does continuous batching allow?
options: All users must finish at the same time
Requests can enter and leave the running workload as generation progresses
Every token bypasses the model
check.explanation: The batch can evolve across iterations, helping use capacity despite requests having different arrival times and lengths.

science.title: Generation latency decomposition
science.explanation: Time to first token covers the initial wait and work; later tokens accumulate inter-token latency. Two systems with equal total throughput can offer very different interactive responsiveness.
science.assumptions: Simplified mean-latency decomposition for one streamed request with at least one output token; actual token gaps and network delivery vary.

history.title: PagedAttention connects memory management to LLM serving
history.significance: The vLLM paper showed how block-based KV-cache management and flexible sharing can improve the use of memory during batched generation. Reported gains depend on workloads and comparisons.

source.title: Kwon et al. — PagedAttention

name: Quantization and numerical representation
role: Represents model values with reduced precision to lower storage and arithmetic costs.
description: Quantization maps values into a limited set of representable levels. For a simple symmetric integer example, divide by a scale, round, and clamp into the available range; dequantization reconstructs an approximation using that scale. Other formats, including low-bit floating point and block-scaled schemes, use different representations. The atlas shows a continuous value distribution landing on discrete levels and makes clipping visible at the extremes. Fewer bits can reduce model storage and data movement, but metadata, scales, unquantized tensors, and execution support affect actual savings. Accuracy must be measured on the intended tasks. Quantization is an engineering tradeoff in representation, not a guarantee that every smaller format preserves the same model behavior.

specs.label: Teaching equation
specs.context: Symmetric integer example with positive scale s.

specs.label: INT8 representation
specs.context: Actual tensors can also need scales and other metadata.

specs.label: Precision choices
specs.context: These need not all use the same format.

tradeoff: Fewer bits reduce some memory and compute costs. Rounding, clipping, and unsupported paths can erase the expected benefit.
whyAI: Lower precision can make models cheaper to serve or train. Quality and performance must be evaluated together on the real workload.
scale: Numerical value-space model; no physical scale
mechanism: Choose a representable range and scaling rule for the selected format.
Map values to allowed levels, including rounding and any clipping.
Execute with supported arithmetic and evaluate output quality and achieved performance.
misconception: An eight-bit weight format does not imply that all activations, accumulators, metadata, or runtime memory use eight bits.

check.question: What happens to a value outside the chosen quantization range?
options: It becomes infinitely precise
It always expands the hardware word size
It may be clipped to the representable boundary
check.explanation: Clipping loses information at the extremes, so scale selection and task-level evaluation matter.

science.title: Unclipped rounding-error bound
science.explanation: Uniform nearest rounding limits each unclipped scalar’s reconstruction error to half a quantization step. Clipping and downstream error propagation are separate and can be much more consequential.
science.assumptions: Positive constant scale, nearest rounding, and values inside the representable range; does not bound end-to-end model error or describe every floating-point/block format.

name: Tokenizer
role: Turn text into a sequence of discrete IDs.
description: Before a text model can compute, its input needs a numerical representation. A tokenizer breaks a byte or character stream into pieces and assigns each piece an integer. Common subword methods represent frequent fragments compactly while retaining a way to encode unfamiliar text. The IDs are addresses, not meaning scores. The same visible word may occupy different numbers of tokens depending on the vocabulary and surrounding text.
mechanism: Encode the input using a fixed vocabulary and segmentation rule.
Produce integer IDs and any required control tokens.
Use each ID to select a row of the embedding table.

specs.label: Unit
specs.context: Vocabulary-specific integer, not a voltage.

specs.label: Granularity
specs.context: A token is not necessarily one word.

tradeoff: A larger vocabulary can shorten sequences while increasing embedding storage. Different languages and encodings have different token efficiency.
whyAI: Token count affects context capacity, attention work, and serving memory.
scale: Logical structure · mapped onto physical hardware
misconception: An integer token ID is not a learned semantic vector; the embedding lookup produces that vector.

check.question: Does one token always equal one word?
options: Yes, for all languages
No; it can be a fragment, punctuation, or other encoded piece
Only during training
check.explanation: Tokenization depends on the tokenizer and text, not a universal word boundary.

science.title: Sequence length is an engineering variable
science.equation: T = |encode(text)|; bytes per token = UTF8_bytes(text) / T
science.explanation: T is the number of token IDs produced by the chosen tokenizer. For the same text, different vocabularies can change T and therefore the attention workload, cache size, and amount of text that fits a context budget. This ratio describes encoding compactness; it does not measure intelligence or semantic information.
science.assumptions: Compare identical text, a specified tokenizer version, and the same treatment of control tokens. There is no universal bytes-per-token constant, especially across languages and code.

history.title: Subword BPE enters neural translation
history.significance: Sennrich, Haddow, and Birch adapted byte-pair segmentation to represent rare words as subword sequences. The preprint appeared in 2015; the conference paper followed at ACL 2016.

source.title: Sennrich et al. — Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units

name: Embedding table
role: Give discrete tokens a trainable numerical representation.
description: An embedding table is a matrix with one row per vocabulary entry. Looking up an ID returns a vector that the rest of the network can transform. These values are learned during training. Related uses can acquire useful geometric relationships, but no single coordinate is guaranteed to have a neat human interpretation. The table lives in memory; its displayed three-dimensional form is a small sample of a much higher-dimensional array.
mechanism: Take a token ID as a row address.
Read the corresponding vector of learned values.
Pass the sequence of vectors into the model with position information.

specs.label: Shape
specs.context: Vocabulary size V; vector width d.

specs.label: Storage
specs.context: Excludes quantization metadata and optimizer state.

tradeoff: Wider vectors increase representation capacity and arithmetic/storage cost. Quantization can reduce bytes per value with numerical tradeoffs.
whyAI: Embeddings connect symbolic input to the matrix computations executed by accelerators.

sources.title: Bengio et al. — A Neural Probabilistic Language Model

scale: Logical structure · mapped onto physical hardware
misconception: The visible vector is not a literal concept stored in one neuron.

check.question: What does an embedding lookup return?
options: A row of learned numerical values
A network packet
A transistor address
check.explanation: The ID indexes a trainable matrix row.

science.title: Lookup is a sparse matrix multiplication
science.equation: e_i = one_hot(i)ᵀ E; E ∈ ℝ^(V×d); ∂ℒ/∂E_j = Σ[t: token_t=j] ∂ℒ/∂e_t
science.explanation: A one-hot row selects exactly one of V embedding vectors, each with d coordinates. Implementations gather that row instead of materializing a giant one-hot matrix. During backpropagation, occurrences of the same token contribute to the gradient of the same shared row.
science.assumptions: The gradient expression covers the input lookup path only. A tied output projection, regularization, or other use of E can add gradients to additional rows; quantization changes physical storage.

history.title: Distributed word representations in a neural language model
history.significance: Bengio and colleagues jointly learned word vectors and a sequence probability model, showing how shared continuous representations could generalize beyond previously observed word sequences.

source.title: Bengio et al. — A Neural Probabilistic Language Model

name: Position representation
role: Make sequence order available to attention.
description: Positional schemes provide explicit order or distance information beyond token content and the attention mask. Position information can be added through embeddings or introduced into the attention computation. Rotary position embeddings rotate pairs of query and key coordinates as a function of position, allowing relative displacement to affect their dot product. This is a mathematical operation on vectors, not a rotating physical device. Position methods and long-context training choices vary across model families.
mechanism: Assign each token its position in the sequence.
Apply the model’s chosen position transformation.
Let attention scores depend on content and positional relationships.

specs.label: RoPE
specs.context: One published approach; not universal.

specs.label: Length
specs.context: A long accepted context does not guarantee perfect recall.

tradeoff: Extending context can require changes in training and position handling. Accepting a longer sequence is different from using all its information reliably.
whyAI: Order distinguishes “dog bites person” from “person bites dog.”
scale: Logical structure · mapped onto physical hardware
misconception: Rotary embeddings rotate numerical coordinates, not memory chips.

check.question: Why add position information?
options: To cool the chip
To make token order available to the computation
To turn every vector into a word
check.explanation: Content alone does not specify where an item occurs in a sequence.

science.title: Relative position from paired rotations
science.explanation: For rotary position embedding, R applies independent two-coordinate rotations. The query at position m and key at n are each transformed, but their dot product depends on the relative offset n−m. Position changes compatibility scores while retaining content in q and k.
science.assumptions: This identity uses matching orthogonal rotations and fixed frequencies on both vectors. It describes standard RoPE, not every positional method; context-extension schemes may modify position or frequency mappings.

history.title: RoFormer proposes rotary position embedding
history.significance: The RoFormer preprint introduced RoPE, encoding position through query/key rotations so their interaction includes relative displacement.

source.title: Su et al. — RoFormer

name: Self-attention
role: Exchange information between token representations.
description: Self-attention computes content-dependent mixtures of information. Learned projections produce queries, keys, and values. Query–key dot products become scores; scaling, a causal mask when appropriate, and softmax turn them into weights. Those weights mix value vectors. Multiple heads can form different mixtures. A causal decoder prevents a position from using future tokens during training. The atlas displays a small matrix so the relationship between rows, columns, and weighted values remains visible.
mechanism: Project representations into Q, K, and V.
Form softmax(QKᵀ / √dₖ + mask).
Multiply the weights by V and combine heads.

specs.label: Dense score shape
specs.context: T is sequence length; algorithms need not store the full matrix.

specs.label: Causality
specs.context: For an autoregressive decoder.

tradeoff: Dense attention has quadratic pairwise work in sequence length. IO-aware kernels reduce memory traffic while implementing the same attention mathematics, subject to finite-precision differences.
whyAI: Attention makes relationships within context available to each token.

sources.title: Vaswani et al. — Attention Is All You Need

scale: Logical structure · mapped onto physical hardware
misconception: Attention weights are not a complete explanation of a model’s reasoning.

check.question: What does the attention weight matrix mix?
options: CPU clocks
Value vectors
Raw electrical power
check.explanation: Each row weights the value vectors available to that query.

science.title: Scaled dot-product attention
science.equation: A = softmax_rows(QKᵀ / √dₖ + M); Y = AV; Var(qᵀk) ≈ dₖ
science.explanation: Each row of A describes how one query mixes allowed value vectors. Dividing by √dₖ controls score scale: a sum of dₖ independent unit-variance products has variance dₖ. Without that adjustment, larger head widths can push softmax toward saturation. The matrix products expose why data reuse matters on GPU tensor units.
science.assumptions: The variance argument assumes independent, zero-mean, unit-variance query/key coordinates; trained vectors need not satisfy it exactly. M is zero for allowed positions and negative infinity for masked positions. This is one attention head before output projection.

history.title: The Transformer replaces recurrent sequence processing
history.significance: Attention Is All You Need demonstrated an encoder–decoder built from attention and position-wise transformations, enabling parallel processing across training positions. It did not establish that attention alone constitutes intelligence.

source.title: Vaswani et al. — Attention Is All You Need

name: Feed-forward network
role: Transform features within each token position.
description: A transformer also applies learned nonlinear transformations to each token representation. A feed-forward block usually expands or projects the vector, applies a nonlinearity or learned gate, and projects it back. It reuses the same parameters at each position. Gated variants such as SwiGLU use one branch to modulate another. The numerical arrays are large, so these transformations account for substantial matrix arithmetic and weight movement.
mechanism: Project a token vector into intermediate features.
Apply the nonlinearity or combine gated branches.
Project back to the residual width.

specs.label: Input/output
specs.context: Residual connections require compatible shapes.

specs.label: Intermediate width
specs.context: No hidden Astra dimensions are assumed.

tradeoff: Wider intermediates increase parameter storage and compute. Sparse expert routing changes which feed-forward weights are used per token.
whyAI: Attention exchanges information; the feed-forward block transforms features.
scale: Logical structure · mapped onto physical hardware
misconception: A network layer is a logical operation; it is not a dedicated physical layer of silicon.

check.question: Are feed-forward weights normally unique to each token position?
options: Yes
No, the block reuses its weights across positions
Only on CPUs
check.explanation: The same learned transformation is applied at different sequence positions.

science.title: SwiGLU and matrix cost
science.explanation: Two projections create dff intermediate features. One branch gates the other coordinate by coordinate, and a third matrix projects back to width d. The three matrices explain both the parameter count and the large repeated matrix multiplications in a gated feed-forward block.
science.assumptions: This is a bias-free SwiGLU example using row vectors, not a universal architecture specification. Wg and Wu have shape d×dff; Wd has shape dff×d. Nonlinear operations, optimizer state, and routing are excluded from the parameter estimate.

history.title: GLU variants improve Transformer feed-forward blocks
history.significance: Shazeer evaluated gated alternatives including SwiGLU and GEGLU in Transformer feed-forward sublayers, finding improvements over the tested ReLU and GELU baselines.

source.title: Shazeer — GLU Variants Improve Transformer

name: Residual stream & normalization
role: Keep a deep sequence of transformations trainable.
description: Residual connections add a block’s output to a continuing representation. This lets each block contribute an update and provides a direct route through a deep computation graph. Normalization controls aspects of numerical scale; LayerNorm uses the mean and variance over specified feature dimensions, while other normalizers differ. Placement before or after sublayers matters. Neither operation creates persistent autobiographical memory: the stream is an intermediate activation for the current computation.
mechanism: Normalize the features at the architecture’s chosen location.
Compute the block’s transformation.
Add the compatible result to the continuing representation.

specs.label: Residual add
specs.context: Both operands must have compatible shapes.

specs.label: LayerNorm
specs.context: Usually includes learned affine parameters.

tradeoff: Normalization and residual placement affect stability. Low precision requires care with accumulation and numerical ranges.
whyAI: These operations make very deep learned transformations practical.

sources.title: He et al. — Deep Residual Learning

scale: Logical structure · mapped onto physical hardware
misconception: Residual streams carry current activations; they are not persistent personal memory.

check.question: What travels through a residual connection?
options: An intermediate numerical representation
An archive of all training documents
Coolant
check.explanation: It carries activations through the computation graph.

science.title: Normalization and a direct gradient route
science.equation: LN(x) = γ ⊙ (x−μ)/√(σ²+ε) + β; y = x + F(x); ∂y/∂x = I + J_F(x)
science.explanation: LayerNorm measures the mean and variance of one representation across its normalized features, then applies learned scale and shift. Separately, a residual add supplies an identity term in the Jacobian, giving gradients a direct path alongside the learned transformation. Neither guarantees that all deep networks train stably.
science.assumptions: The residual equation describes an identity skip with matching shapes; F may include normalization. LayerNorm uses population variance over the chosen features. RMSNorm omits mean subtraction, and pre-norm versus post-norm changes the full block Jacobian.

history.title: Layer normalization removes dependence on batch statistics
history.significance: Ba, Kiros, and Hinton proposed normalization within a training example, with the same normalization computation at training and inference. This became useful for sequence models with varying batch conditions.

source.title: Ba et al. — Layer Normalization

name: Output head & decoding
role: Convert the final representation into the next token.
description: The output projection assigns a logit to each candidate vocabulary token. A softmax can turn these scores into a probability distribution, after which a decoding rule selects an output. Greedy decoding takes a maximum; sampling introduces controlled randomness. The chosen ID is appended to the sequence and the process continues. A fluent output is therefore produced by many repeated computations, with behavior influenced by training, context, decoding, and any external tools.
mechanism: Project the final hidden representation to vocabulary logits.
Apply the decoding policy to select a token ID.
Append that token and compute the next step.

specs.label: Logits
specs.context: One score per vocabulary entry.

specs.label: Autoregression
specs.context: Batching and speculative methods alter execution scheduling.

interfaces.name: User / next step
interfaces.signal: Selected token ID and decoded text

tradeoff: Sampling changes diversity and reproducibility. Output probability is not a calibrated guarantee that a statement is true.
whyAI: Repeated decoding turns numerical transformations into an interactive response.

sources.title: Brown et al. — Language Models are Few-Shot Learners

scale: Logical structure · mapped onto physical hardware
misconception: The output head chooses vocabulary symbols; factual verification requires additional evidence.

check.question: Does a high next-token probability establish factual truth?
options: Yes
No
Only with more GPUs
check.explanation: The distribution reflects the trained prediction task and context.

science.title: A sequence probability factors into conditional predictions
science.equation: p(x₁,…,xT) = ∏ₜ p(xₜ | x<t); p(xₜ=i | x<t) = exp(z_i)/Σⱼexp(z_j)
science.explanation: The chain rule factors a joint sequence distribution into conditional steps. Vocabulary logits z become normalized next-token probabilities. Greedy or sampling-based selection then turns the distribution into a particular sequence. A likely continuation can still assert something false, because probability under a language model is not a truth certificate.
science.assumptions: This is a standard autoregressive categorical decoder. It does not specify any model’s exposed sampling controls or internal scheduling; speculative decoding can verify several proposed tokens together while preserving a target distribution.

history.title: GPT-3 demonstrates broad in-context task conditioning
history.significance: Brown and colleagues evaluated GPT-3 on many tasks using textual instructions and examples without task-specific gradient updates, illustrating the difference between conditioning generation and retraining weights.

source.title: Brown et al. — Language Models are Few-Shot Learners

name: Key–value cache
role: Reuse earlier attention state during generation.
description: An autoregressive transformer would waste work if it recomputed every previous key and value at each step. A KV cache stores these intermediate arrays for later attention. It is distinct from model weights and from a hardware cache such as L2. Its size grows with the active sequence and batch, and depends strongly on the number of key–value heads and precision. Serving systems manage these arrays across changing requests, often with block-based allocation.
mechanism: Store each new token’s keys and values for every relevant layer.
Read the past cache when computing the next token’s attention.
Release or reuse allocation when a request finishes.

specs.label: Payload estimate
specs.value: 2 × B × L × T × Hkv × Dh × s
specs.context: Uniform uncompressed full-attention payload: batch B, layers L, tokens T, KV heads Hkv, head width Dh, and s bytes/value; excludes allocation overhead.

specs.label: Scope
specs.context: Not a permanent update to trained weights.

tradeoff: More context and concurrent requests consume memory. Quantization, grouped-query attention, and allocation policies change the cost.
whyAI: KV memory often limits long-context serving concurrency.
scale: Logical structure · mapped onto physical hardware
misconception: The KV cache is a software-managed tensor, not the chip’s hardware cache.

check.question: Does adding a token to the KV cache retrain the model?
options: Yes
Only at night
No
check.explanation: It stores inference intermediates; the learned weights are unchanged.

science.title: The cache grows with every retained position
science.equation: M_KV = 2·B·L·T·Hkv·Dh·s bytes; ΔM per token per sequence = 2·L·Hkv·Dh·s
science.explanation: The factor two counts keys and values. Multiply sequences B, cached layers L, retained positions T, KV heads Hkv, head width Dh, and bytes per value s. Sharing one KV head among several query heads reduces this payload without requiring the same reduction in query heads.
science.assumptions: This uniform full-attention estimate assumes equal key/value widths and sequence lengths, no prefix sharing, no replication, and no compression or allocator overhead. Sliding-window and hybrid models need a layer-by-layer sum. It is not an estimate of Astra’s hidden architecture.

history.title: PagedAttention reorganizes inference memory
history.significance: Kwon and colleagues described a paged KV-cache layout that reduces fragmentation and supports sharing, connecting language-model serving to operating-system memory-management ideas.

source.title: Kwon et al. — Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention

name: Mixture of experts
role: Route each token to a subset of learned transformations.
description: A mixture-of-experts layer contains several expert networks and a router. The router selects a small subset for each token, then the system combines their outputs. Total stored parameters can therefore grow faster than the arithmetic used for one token. This creates an infrastructure problem: expert weights need capacity, routing can be imbalanced, and tokens may travel between devices. The experts are numerical functions, not independently conscious specialists.
mechanism: Score expert choices for each token.
Dispatch tokens to selected experts, possibly across devices.
Combine outputs and return them to the continuing representation.

specs.label: Active vs total
specs.context: Only selected experts execute per token.

specs.label: Communication
specs.context: Depends on expert placement and implementation.

tradeoff: Sparse activation saves arithmetic relative to activating every expert, but increases routing and load-balancing complexity.
whyAI: Model design and network topology become tightly connected.
scale: Logical structure · mapped onto physical hardware
misconception: An expert is a learned computation, not a separate humanlike mind.

check.question: Why can an MoE model have many stored but fewer active parameters?
options: Only selected experts run for each token
Its memory is imaginary
All expert weights disappear after training
check.explanation: Routing selects a subset of the available expert networks.

science.title: Stored capacity versus activated computation
science.equation: y = Σ[i∈S(x)] g_i(x)E_i(x); N_total = N_shared + E·N_expert; N_active ≈ N_shared + k·N_expert
science.explanation: A router selects a set S(x) containing k of E experts. The selected outputs receive routing weights g_i. With equally sized experts, increasing E can enlarge stored capacity without multiplying the number of expert matrices evaluated for each token. Communication and routing still consume real time.
science.assumptions: This is a simplified top-k layer with equal expert sizes. Routing weights may be renormalized differently, capacity limits can drop or reroute tokens, and shared experts alter the count. Parameter activation is not a complete FLOP or latency model.

history.title: Switch Transformer simplifies sparse routing
history.significance: The Switch Transformer preprint investigated top-one expert routing and training techniques that made very large sparse Transformer models easier to train; it was published in JMLR in 2022.

source.title: Fedus et al. — Switch Transformers

name: Training data pipeline
role: Convert a source collection into useful learning examples.
description: A training pipeline may collect, filter, deduplicate, format, tokenize, and batch data. The mixture controls which patterns the optimizer repeatedly encounters. Quality is not a single scalar: correctness, coverage, provenance, licensing, contamination, and representativeness all matter. Training, validation, and benchmark splits need careful separation and overlap checks. More bytes alone do not guarantee better learning; repeated low-value or contaminated examples can waste compute and distort evaluation.
mechanism: Prepare and document the source mixture.
Filter, deduplicate, tokenize, and form batches.
Track validation and contamination separately from optimization.

specs.label: Budget
specs.context: Different from raw corpus size.

specs.label: Data quality
specs.context: Coverage, correctness, provenance, and duplication matter.

interfaces.name: Training loop
interfaces.signal: Batches of token IDs and targets

tradeoff: Cleaning can remove useful rare content as well as noise. Data composition must match intended capabilities and evaluation goals.
whyAI: Data supplies the examples that shape the model’s learned behavior.

sources.title: Lee et al. — Deduplicating Training Data Makes Language Models Better

scale: Logical structure · mapped onto physical hardware
misconception: Training tokens are not the same thing as a count of unique source documents.

check.question: Does a larger raw corpus guarantee a better model?
options: No; quality and training use matter
Yes, without exception
Only if it contains images
check.explanation: Size alone misses duplication, usefulness, coverage, and optimization.

science.title: The mixture defines the expected learning signal
science.explanation: Each data source D_j contributes according to its sampling weight w_j. Changing those weights changes which errors the optimizer is asked to reduce most often. Repeating near-duplicates can therefore increase their influence without adding comparable diversity. The same nominal token budget can represent very different learning opportunities.
science.assumptions: This expectation assumes a fixed mixture and loss definition. Curriculum schedules, example weighting, repeated epochs, and adaptive sampling modify the effective weights. Source quality and legal provenance cannot be inferred from the equation.

history.title: Deduplication is measured as a training intervention
history.significance: Lee and colleagues showed that removing repeated training material could reduce memorized output and train–test overlap while preserving or improving measured accuracy. Their preprint preceded ACL 2022 publication.

source.title: Lee et al. — Deduplicating Training Data Makes Language Models Better

name: Loss, gradients & optimizer
role: Turn prediction errors into parameter updates.
description: A loss assigns a numerical training objective to the model’s predictions. Backpropagation applies the chain rule through the computation graph to obtain gradients. An optimizer uses those gradients and, often, additional state to update weights. Adam maintains estimates related to gradient moments. This backward computation and optimizer storage distinguish training from ordinary inference. Distributed execution must coordinate the appropriate gradients or shards before consistent updates can proceed.
mechanism: Run the forward computation and evaluate the loss.
Backpropagate derivatives through the recorded operations.
Combine required distributed information and update parameters.

specs.label: Gradient
specs.context: Local sensitivity of the objective.

specs.label: Adam state
specs.context: Adds storage beyond the weights.

tradeoff: Optimizer state and saved activations consume substantial memory. Checkpointing can exchange extra computation for lower activation storage.
whyAI: Learning is an optimization process executed by physical arithmetic and memory systems.
scale: Logical structure · mapped onto physical hardware
misconception: Backpropagation computes derivatives; the optimizer decides the update.

check.question: Which process changes learned weights in a normal training step?
options: Displaying a response
Applying an optimizer update
Reading a KV cache
check.explanation: The optimizer updates parameters using gradients and its update rule.

science.title: Adam adapts updates using gradient moments
science.equation: gₜ = ∇θℒₜ; mₜ = β₁mₜ₋₁+(1−β₁)gₜ; vₜ = β₂vₜ₋₁+(1−β₂)gₜ²; θₜ₊₁ = θₜ−η·m̂ₜ/(√v̂ₜ+ε)
science.explanation: The first moment m smooths gradient direction; the second moment v tracks squared gradient magnitude. Bias-corrected estimates m̂ and v̂ scale each coordinate’s step. The optimizer consequently needs state arrays in addition to weights and gradients, connecting a mathematical update rule directly to accelerator memory requirements.
science.assumptions: Products, squares, and divisions are coordinate-wise. With zero initialization, m̂ₜ=mₜ/(1−β₁ᵗ) and v̂ₜ=vₜ/(1−β₂ᵗ). This is ordinary Adam; decoupled weight decay, clipping, loss scaling, and distributed sharding require additional rules.

history.title: Adam combines momentum with adaptive scaling
history.significance: Kingma and Ba released the Adam preprint in December 2014; its conference publication followed at ICLR 2015. The method maintains first and second gradient-moment estimates.

source.title: Kingma & Ba — Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization

name: Post-training & feedback
role: Shape a pretrained model into an assistant.
description: Pretraining builds broad predictive capability. Further supervised examples, preference learning, reinforcement learning, and other objectives can then change behavior toward useful instruction following and task performance. These methods alter model weights; a prompt alone normally does not. Feedback quality and evaluation design become central because optimizing a proxy can reward unwanted shortcuts. Different systems use different recipes, and the atlas does not assign a private recipe to Astra.
mechanism: Collect demonstrations or task-specific feedback.
Optimize against the chosen supervision or reward signal.
Evaluate generalization and unintended behavior on held-out tasks.

specs.label: Stage
specs.context: May include multiple training phases.

specs.label: Feedback
specs.context: Feedback need not be objectively verifiable; the method determines how it is used.

tradeoff: A reward is a proxy for the intended behavior. Improvements on one evaluation can coexist with regressions elsewhere.
whyAI: Post-training connects broad modeling ability to more useful interactive behavior.
scale: Logical structure · mapped onto physical hardware
misconception: Instruction following is learned behavior, not proof of perfect reliability.

check.question: How does post-training differ from adding a prompt?
options: It normally changes weights through training
It merely changes the screen color
It requires no examples or objective
check.explanation: Post-training performs optimization; prompting supplies inference context.

science.title: Reward optimization with a reference penalty
science.explanation: One reinforcement-learning formulation rewards useful responses while penalizing excessive movement from a reference policy. The reward r is an operational training signal; optimizing it need not maximize every property people care about. The KL term makes the tradeoff explicit rather than eliminating reward-model error.
science.assumptions: This is an idealized core RLHF objective with β≥0. It omits auxiliary pretraining losses and optimizer details. Supervised fine-tuning, direct preference optimization, and learning from verifiable rewards can use different objectives; no private Astra recipe is implied.

history.title: InstructGPT combines demonstrations and preferences
history.significance: Ouyang and colleagues reported supervised instruction tuning followed by preference-based reinforcement learning, showing that user preference could improve without merely increasing parameter count.

source.title: Ouyang et al. — Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback

name: Tools, memory & agent loop
role: Connect model inference to actions and evidence.
description: A model can propose a structured tool call, but a surrounding runtime must validate it, execute the tool, and return the result. The next model invocation can use that observation. Search, code execution, file operations, and external memory are therefore parts of a larger system around the neural network. Permissions, state tracking, error handling, and verification determine what the system can do reliably. A retrieved document and a model parameter are different kinds of memory.
mechanism: Interpret the task and generate a response or proposed action.
Execute an allowed tool through the runtime and capture its result.
Use observations to revise the plan, continue, or finish.

specs.label: Boundary
specs.context: Tools execute outside the weight matrices.

specs.label: Persistence
specs.context: External memory differs from a context window.

tradeoff: More tools expand reach while increasing dependencies and failure modes. Useful autonomy requires measurable completion and recovery behavior.
whyAI: Advanced assistants combine learned inference with software and infrastructure.
scale: Logical structure · mapped onto physical hardware
misconception: Tool access is a system capability, not a new physical neuron inside the model.

check.question: What actually executes a model-proposed tool call?
options: A surrounding runtime or application
The embedding table itself
A silicon atom
check.explanation: The model emits a proposal; software carries out the operation and returns observations.

science.title: A closed loop changes context and the environment
science.equation: aₜ ∼ πθ(·|hₜ); oₜ = Tool(aₜ); hₜ₊₁ = Update(hₜ,aₜ,oₜ)
science.explanation: The model conditions an action proposal a on available history h. A runtime executes an allowed tool and returns an observation o. The next invocation receives updated context and can change its next action. This creates feedback with the world while ordinary inference keeps the trained parameters θ fixed.
science.assumptions: This is a schematic sequential loop, not a hidden implementation. Tools may fail, be asynchronous, or change external state; the runtime enforces permissions and can decline actions. Context management may summarize rather than retain all history.

history.title: ReAct interleaves language-model reasoning and actions
history.significance: Yao and colleagues explored alternating reasoning and actions that gather observations from external environments. The preprint appeared in 2022 and the conference version at ICLR 2023.

source.title: Yao et al. — ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

name: Scaling laws & resource allocation
role: Understand how data, parameters, and compute interact.
description: Scaling studies fit empirical relationships between training resources and predictive loss over measured regimes. They help estimate how to allocate a compute budget between model size and training data. For a decreasing power-law excess loss, a fixed resource multiplier produces a smaller absolute loss reduction at larger scales; exponential growth in available compute is a separate claim about resources over time. Neither relationship is a proof that general intelligence arrives at a specific date. Algorithms, data quality, hardware efficiency, and inference-time work also matter.
mechanism: Measure comparable models across controlled resource budgets.
Fit and test a relationship within the observed regime.
Use the estimate to plan a new run, then validate the result.

specs.label: Power law
specs.context: Illustrative form; fitted constants are regime dependent.

specs.label: Compute allocation
specs.context: Simple dense-model estimates omit many real costs.

tradeoff: Extrapolation gets less trustworthy beyond measured regimes. Loss reduction and broad capability are related but not interchangeable.
whyAI: Scaling explains part of the arc from early GPTs to larger systems, alongside algorithmic progress.
scale: Logical structure · mapped onto physical hardware
misconception: Exponential resource growth is not the same claim as an exponential improvement in every capability.

check.question: Do scaling laws establish a guaranteed AGI date?
options: Yes
No; they are empirical relationships over measured regimes
Only from transistor count
check.explanation: They guide resource allocation; they do not prove an AGI timeline.

science.title: Compute-optimal balance is an empirical fit
science.equation: ℒ(N,D) ≈ ℒ∞ + A/Nᵅ + B/Dᵝ; C ≈ 6ND; N_opt ∝ C^[β/(α+β)]; D_opt ∝ C^[α/(α+β)]
science.explanation: N denotes model parameters and D training tokens. Under the fitted loss model and fixed compute C, spending everything on either dimension leaves the other as a bottleneck. Minimizing the two error terms yields the allocation exponents shown. These are planning relationships for measured regimes, not a law mapping FLOPs to general intelligence.
science.assumptions: Positive fitted constants and exponents; dense Transformer parameter-dominated training. The 6ND approximation counts forward and backward matrix work and omits important long-context, embedding, communication, and system costs. Data quality, architecture, and objective must remain sufficiently comparable.

history.title: Chinchilla revisits compute-optimal model and data scaling
history.significance: Hoffmann and colleagues found that their compute-optimal runs called for growing training tokens alongside parameters, challenging an emphasis on ever-larger models with comparatively fixed data budgets.

source.title: Hoffmann et al. — Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models

name: Evaluation & the AGI frontier
role: Measure breadth, reliability, and practical competence.
description: A useful evaluation asks what the entire system can accomplish under clear conditions. It records correctness, consistency, cost, latency, tool access, and the amount of human help allowed. Generality involves breadth across tasks and transfer to unfamiliar situations; excellent results on one benchmark cannot establish all of it. Contamination and benchmark saturation complicate comparison. This atlas ends at an open research frontier: the assembled machinery enables increasingly capable systems, while the definition and demonstration of AGI require explicit evidence.
mechanism: Define tasks, success criteria, and permitted resources.
Test on held-out and unfamiliar cases, including failures.
Report uncertainty, repeatability, and limits alongside successes.

specs.label: Dimensions
specs.context: A framework, not a single universal score.

specs.label: Evidence
specs.context: Benchmark conditions affect conclusions.

tradeoff: A compact benchmark is easy to compare but cannot cover all real-world situations. More representative evaluation costs time and effort.
whyAI: The goal is useful, reliable competence; larger machines are a means to test, not proof of the goal.

sources.title: Morris et al. — Levels of AGI

scale: Logical structure · mapped onto physical hardware
misconception: An impressive system architecture does not, by itself, establish general intelligence.

check.question: What does strong performance on one benchmark demonstrate?
options: Universal AGI by itself
Performance on that benchmark under its stated conditions
That evaluation is no longer needed
check.explanation: Breadth, reliability, and transfer require additional evidence.

science.title: Benchmark success has sampling uncertainty
science.explanation: If k of n independently sampled tasks succeed, p̂ estimates the success probability for that task distribution. The estimated standard error shrinks only as the square root of sample size: roughly four times as many comparable trials are needed to halve it. This uncertainty says nothing by itself about tasks outside the tested distribution.
science.assumptions: Binary outcomes, independent trials, fixed conditions, and a representative sample are required. The plug-in approximation is poor near zero or one or with small n; use suitable binomial intervals. Correlated tasks, benchmark selection, contamination, and judge error add other uncertainties.

history.title: Levels of AGI separates breadth from performance
history.significance: Morris and colleagues proposed a framework for comparing capability breadth and performance while treating deployment autonomy separately, making progress claims more explicit than a single benchmark score.

source.title: Morris et al. — Levels of AGI for Operationalizing Progress on the Path to AGI

name: GPT-6 Astra
role: Connect documented model capabilities to a larger system of context, tools, and evaluation.
description: GPT-6 Astra is the named model at this atlas’s contemporary endpoint. OpenAI documents support for reasoning, coding, research, computer use, and document creation, with text input/output and image input. Its published API limits describe the service interface. They do not disclose a parameter count, layer count, attention layout, training cluster, or physical deployment. The surrounding application supplies context, tools, and execution controls. The earlier anatomical views teach published mechanisms and reference hardware, while this view shows the boundary between those concepts and what is actually documented for Astra.
mechanism: An application assembles instructions, input, prior context, and permitted tools.
Astra generates a response or tool calls; a runtime handles allowed actions and returns results.
The application presents the result and evaluates it against the task’s actual success criteria.

specs.label: API context window
specs.context: Official GPT-6 Astra model reference, verified September 6, 2026; client applications can impose their own limits.

specs.label: Maximum API output
specs.context: Generated-token budget includes reasoning and other counted generated tokens, not only visible prose.

specs.label: Modalities
specs.context: Native audio and video are listed as unsupported; separate tools can supply additional media capabilities.

specs.label: Structured interaction
specs.context: Tool calling requires the Responses API, according to the September 3, 2026 changelog.

interfaces.name: Application context
interfaces.signal: Instructions, text, images, and supplied tool results

interfaces.name: Application runtime
interfaces.signal: Generated responses and supported structured tool calls

tradeoff: A larger accepted context creates room for more material, but reliable use of that material remains task-dependent. Tools extend what an application can accomplish while adding execution, state-management, and verification requirements.
whyAI: Astra provides a concrete present-day interface for exploring how a learned model and a surrounding runtime work together. Its public limits give learners measurable specifications without presenting an imagined internal blueprint.

sources.title: OpenAI — Reasoning Models: Context and Output Accounting

scale: Public model-service interface · physical internals undisclosed
misconception: A published context length is a token-budget specification; it does not reveal the number of layers, model parameters, GPUs, or an AGI threshold.

check.question: What does Astra’s published context limit establish?
options: A bound on the documented API token context
Its exact parameter count and GPU allocation
Perfect recall and general intelligence
check.explanation: The reference specifies an interface limit. Architecture and task reliability require separate evidence.

science.title: Visible output shares a generated-token budget
science.equation: G = R + V + F; I + G ≤ C; G ≤ O_max
science.explanation: I is the counted input context, R generated reasoning tokens, V visible output tokens, and F other counted generated formatting tokens. C is the context limit and O_max the effective output cap. Reserving output room therefore requires accounting for more than the prose the user sees.
science.assumptions: A simplified budget for one model sampling segment with fixed input; use actual API token accounting and configured limits. Tool loops, retained reasoning, multimodal tokenization, and compaction affect later segments. These symbols do not describe hidden model dimensions.

history.title: GPT-6 Astra released through the OpenAI API
history.significance: The September 3 API changelog announced Astra for complex tasks using supplied context and tools, with tool calling through the Responses API. This is a product milestone, not a declaration of AGI.

source.title: OpenAI API Changelog — September 3, 2026
